section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a narrow road when meeting an oncoming vehicle, what must you do?
options: a:Demand the other vehicle pull over.,b:Pull completely off the road and stop.,c:Allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road.
note: On narrow roads, give oncoming traffic at least half of the main-traveled portion so both vehicles can pass safely.

question: It is an infraction to smoke in a vehicle when a child is present.
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: You may not smoke in a vehicle while transporting a child age 15 or younger; doing so is an infraction.

question: Approaching a heavy truck from behind while driving uphill, you should know:
options: a:You may not be able to safely pass the truck.,b:The truck may be traveling at a speed slower than the posted limit.,c:You may not be able to legally pass the truck.
note: Large vehicles often slow when climbing hills; be cautious approaching them and avoid unsafe passing where visibility is limited.

question: What does a steady yellow arrow at a signal mean?
options: a:Merge into the lane indicated by the arrow immediately.,b:Prepare to stop because a red arrow is coming.,c:You may turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic.
note: A steady yellow arrow warns that the signal is about to change to red; stop if you can do so safely.

question: When in line of traffic crossing a railroad without signals, what must you ensure?
options: a:You may pass slower drivers while on the tracks.,b:You have the right-of-way and need not check for trains.,c:There is enough space for your vehicle to fully clear the tracks.
note: Before entering tracks, make sure you have room to clear them completely; never pass another vehicle while crossing.

question: If a fire engine follows you but has no lights/sirens on, how should you respond?
options: a:Pull over immediately.,b:Continue driving normally.,c:Speed up to clear the way.
note: If an emergency vehicle is not using emergency signals, you are not required to yield; keep driving normally.

question: A red and white triangular sign at an intersection means:
options: a:Always come to a full stop at the intersection.,b:Look both ways as you cross the intersection.,c:Yield and be prepared to stop if necessary.
note: A yield sign requires you to slow and give right-of-way to vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection, stopping if necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it permissible to stop in a travel lane to drop off passengers or to look up an address?
options: a:Yes — you may stop to drop off passengers.,b:No — you should not stop in a travel lane for any reason.,c:Yes — you may stop to look up an address.
note: Do not stop in a travel lane. If you miss a turn or exit, continue to the next safe place to turn around rather than stopping or backing up in the lane.

question: What color are pavement markings that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Blue,b:White,c:Red,d:Yellow
note: Yellow pavement markings are used to separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

question: Traffic lanes moving in opposite directions are divided by what color lines?
options: a:White,b:Black,c:Yellow
note: Yellow pavement markings divide traffic moving in opposite directions.

question: What should you avoid when driving on slippery roads?
options: a:Reducing your following distance.,b:Using cruise control.,c:Driving below the speed limit.
note: Do not use cruise control on slippery roads; also reduce speed and avoid sudden movements to maintain control.

question: Why should you be particularly cautious when passing a bicycle?
options: a:You are moving faster than the bicycle.,b:The bicycle always has the right-of-way.,c:Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass the bicycle.
note: Cyclists may swerve to avoid road hazards, and oncoming drivers may not anticipate you moving into the opposite lane to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your freeway exit and want to get off, you should:
options: a:Proceed to the next exit and safely leave the freeway,b:Make a U-turn across the median,c:Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit,d:Cross multiple lanes quickly to reach the exit
note: If you miss an exit, take the next exit and return safely. Backing up or crossing medians on freeways is illegal and dangerous.

question: When driving in fog, which actions are recommended?
options: a:Drive at the posted speed but turn on the high beams,b:Use high beam headlights to increase visibility,c:Drive cautiously at reduced speed and use low beam headlights (do not use high beams),d:Ignore fog and continue as normal
note: In fog, slow down, use low beams (or fog lights), and avoid high beams which can worsen visibility by reflecting light back.

question: A traffic signal showing a green arrow with a red light means you may:
options: a:You must wait for a solid green to proceed in any direction.,b:You may drive only in the direction of the green arrow.,c:You may only drive straight ahead.
note: A green arrow permits movement only in the arrow's direction, even if other signals are red, provided the intersection is clear.

question: What problems do worn or bald tires create?
options: a:Only reduced fuel efficiency.,b:No effect on handling in dry conditions.,c:Increased stopping distance
note: Tires with little tread increase stopping distance, make turning harder, and raise hydroplaning risk.

question: A driver behind a motorcycle must allow as much following distance as when following a car. True or False?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Motorcyclists can stop or maneuver more quickly; allow at least three to four seconds following distance to give them room to react.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which pavement line allows you to pass another vehicle traveling in the same direction?
options: a:Double solid yellow lines,b:A single solid white line,c:A solid yellow line beside your lane,d:A broken white line
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to change lanes or pass when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your vehicle's turn signals fail, you should use which method to indicate turns?
options: a:Hand signals,b:Your horn,c:Your headlights
note: Use hand signals to indicate turns if your electric turn signals are not functioning.

question: Which of these is least helpful for safe night driving?
options: a:Carrying a flashlight in your vehicle,b:Keeping the windshield clean,c:Being aware that tinted windows reduce night visibility,d:Reducing interior reflections by cleaning glass
note: Carrying a flashlight may be useful in emergencies but does not directly improve night driving safety like clean glass or reduced interior reflections do.

question: Why should drivers be extra alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?
options: a:They always have the right-of-way.,b:They are often more difficult to see in traffic.,c:They obey different traffic laws than larger motor vehicles.
note: Smaller road users are harder to detect in traffic due to size and less visible lighting; remain vigilant to avoid collisions.

question: When following another vehicle at night, you must dim your headlights within what distance?
options: a:100 feet.,b:200 feet.,c:300 feet.
note: Dim your high beams to low beams when you are within 300 feet of the vehicle ahead.

question: You must yield to children playing in the street.
options: a:False,b:True
note: Drive with extreme caution where children are present and yield when necessary to protect them.

question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic accidents?
options: a:Excessive speed for conditions.,b:Following other vehicles too closely.,c:Inattentive driving.
note: While all are common causes, driving too fast for the conditions is a major factor in many crashes.

question: When entering a street from a driveway, what must you do?
options: a:Honk to warn others and proceed slowly.,b:Drive slowly through without stopping.,c:Stop and go only when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
note: You must stop before entering the roadway from a driveway, yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic, and not cross the sidewalk area without stopping.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before passing on a multi-lane highway, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up and pass in one quick move,b:Rely only on your mirrors to make the lane change,c:Check that the passing lane is clear and signal before changing lanes,d:Always pass on the right regardless of lane markings
note: Before passing or changing lanes you should confirm the lane is clear, signal your intention, and move over safely.

question: Which factor most directly affects braking distance?
options: a:The condition of the pavement.,b:The condition of your brakes and tires.,c:The speed at which your vehicle is traveling.
note: Braking distance increases rapidly with speed; other factors like brake/tire condition and pavement also affect stopping distance.

question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, what must you do?
options: a:Drive with your flashers on.,b:Slow down until it passes you.,c:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle is approaching with a siren, you must pull over to the curb or side of the road and stop to allow it to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must signal in which of the following situations?
options: a:When pulling into or out of a parking space.,b:When changing lanes.,c:Any time you are turning or changing lanes (all of the above).
note: Signals must be used whenever you change lanes, turn, or pull into/out of parking areas to inform other road users.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on an interstate expressway, you should:
options: a:Get off at the next exit and return safely.,b:Roll down your window and ask the driver next to you for help.,c:Stop and make a U-turn.
note: Do not reverse or make unsafe turns on the highway. Continue to the next exit and safely turn around there.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, which practice is usually best?
options: a:Turn on your hazard lights until you are safely on the freeway.,b:Proceed slowly while waiting for an opening.,c:Accelerate on the ramp to match the speed of freeway traffic and merge safely.
note: Use the acceleration lane to reach traffic speed and merge smoothly; traffic on the freeway has the right-of-way.

question: You are involved in an accident and another person is injured. What should you do?
options: a:Move the injured away from the scene immediately.,b:Always leave the injured where they are.,c:Not move the injured unnecessarily; keep them warm and provide first aid if qualified.
note: Avoid moving injured persons unless absolutely necessary; keep them warm and administer first aid for severe bleeding while waiting for emergency responders.

question: How does increasing your vehicle's speed affect your field of vision?
options: a:Increases your field of vision.,b:Makes it easier to see cross traffic.,c:Decreases your field of vision.
note: As speed increases your field of vision narrows, so you must be more alert to potential hazards.

question: When is it appropriate to honk your horn?
options: a:When passing a bicyclist.,b:When traveling through an intersection.,c:When you see a child who is about to run into the street.
note: Use your horn as a warning to alert others (for example, to stop a child from running into the street), not for routine driving maneuvers.

question: What should you do first to slow on a slippery surface?
options: a:Engage the parking brake.,b:Firmly apply the brakes.,c:Take your foot off the gas.
note: On slippery roads, first ease off the accelerator; apply brakes gently if more deceleration is needed.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow mean on a traffic signal?
options: a:You may turn immediately without caution.,b:It never appears on real signals.,c:It has the same meaning as a circular yellow light — prepare to stop.
note: A solid yellow arrow means the protected turning interval is ending; slow and prepare to stop for red.

question: A flashing red signal at an intersection is equivalent to which sign?
options: a:A yield sign.,b:A stop sign.,c:A slow sign.
note: A flashing red light requires a full stop and yielding to traffic like a stop sign.

question: Only vehicles displaying special plates or placards for persons with disabilities may park in spaces reserved by official sign.
options: a:False,b:True
note: Parking spaces marked for persons with disabilities may only be used by vehicles displaying the appropriate plates or placards.

question: When is it especially important to slow down?
options: a:Only at night,b:Only when you see a speed limit sign,c:Only during heavy traffic,d:On narrow or winding roads
note: Reduce speed on narrow/winding roads, near intersections and crossings, and whenever the road surface is slippery or hazardous.

question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:Mechanical failures,b:Wildlife on roadways,c:Bad weather,d:Human error by drivers
note: Most crashes are caused by human error — mistakes, inattention, poor decisions — rather than unavoidable mechanical reasons.

question: Does drinking coffee after alcohol reduce blood alcohol concentration?
options: a:Yes,b:You yes,c:No
note: Coffee may make you more alert but does not lower blood alcohol concentration or make you sober.

question: When you hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle using lights or siren, you must:
options: a:Drive to the right and stop until it passes.,b:Slow down but remain in your lane.,c:Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass you.
note: Yield right-of-way to emergency vehicles with lights or sirens by pulling to the right and stopping; if in an intersection, clear it first.

question: When driving on wet pavement, remember that:
options: a:Pavement is especially slippery right after it starts to rain.,b:Wet roads cannot cause hydroplaning.,c:You do not need extra space when stopping.
note: Road surfaces are often most slippery in the first few minutes of rain because oil and residue rise to the surface; slow down and increase following distance.

question: If you are involved in a serious motor vehicle crash, what actions should you take?
options: a:Only exchange insurance information and leave immediately,b:Leave the scene and report it later,c:Stop,d:Keep driving to the nearest service station
note: Stop and, if possible, move the vehicle out of traffic. Call emergency services for injuries and report crashes per the state requirements.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, where should you complete the turn?
options: a:Into the left lane of the one-way street,b:Into the center of the street,c:Into the right lane of the one-way street,d:Into any lane that looks clear
note: When turning left onto a one-way street, complete the turn into the leftmost lane that is safe and available.

question: If convicted of driving without insurance, how long must you carry SR-22 in Utah?
options: a:Six months.,b:One year.,c:Three years.
note: A conviction for driving uninsured requires an SR-22 filing and proof of insurance for three years and a reinstatement fee.

question: Can large vehicles have blind spots extending far behind them?
options: a:Trucks always have rear sensors that eliminate blind spots,b:True — blind spots can extend up to 200 feet behind large vehicles,c:False — their mirrors cover the rear,d:Only small vehicles have large blind spots
note: Large trucks have significant blind zones behind them; do not tailgate a large vehicle because the driver likely cannot see you.

question: If an approaching driver fails to dim high beams, where should you look?
options: a:Toward the right side of the road.,b:Straight ahead at the approaching vehicle.,c:At the vehicle's wheels.
note: Glance to the right edge of the road to avoid being blinded while keeping enough view to stay on course.

question: If you borrow an unfamiliar vehicle, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Ignore minor defects to avoid embarrassment,b:Hide from the owner that you are unfamiliar with the car,c:Assume all vehicles work the same and drive immediately,d:Familiarize yourself with the controls and correct any obvious defects
note: When driving an unfamiliar vehicle, learn where the lights, wipers, signals, brakes, and other controls are and correct any safety defects before driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: True or false: You may pass on a two‑lane roadway when the center line next to your lane is a single solid yellow line.
options: a:True — a single solid yellow always allows passing,b:True — if no oncoming traffic is present,c:Only if the other lane is clear,d:False — you may not pass when the line beside your lane is solid
note: You may not cross a solid yellow line to pass; passing is allowed only when the line beside your lane is broken (dashed).

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a stop sign that is not marked by a crosswalk, drivers should stop their vehicles before entering the intersection. True or False?
options: a:False,b:True
note: If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection and yield as required.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, you should:
options: a:Overcorrect to regain control.,b:Steer in the direction of the skid.,c:Turn the wheel into oncoming traffic.
note: If you start to skid, stay calm and steer gently in the direction the vehicle is sliding.

question: A child must remain in a rear-facing car seat until they are at least what age?
options: a:Three years old,b:Four years old,c:Two years old
note: Children should ride in rear-facing car seats until at least two years old or until they exceed the seat's height/weight limits.

question: A solid white edge line on the right that slants toward the center of the road indicates:
options: a:You will be required to turn left just ahead.,b:The road will become narrower ahead.,c:There is an intersection just ahead.
note: An edge line that angles toward the center warns that the roadway narrows ahead, marking the boundary between travel lane and shoulder.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A posted speed limit indicates:
options: a:The exact speed you must travel to avoid a ticket.,b:The maximum legal speed under ideal road and weather conditions.,c:Only a recommended driving speed.
note: A speed limit is the maximum legal speed for ideal conditions; drivers must slow down for poor conditions or hazards.

question: How should you check blind spots before changing lanes?
options: a:By turning your head to physically check the blind spot.,b:Only by using the inside rearview mirror.,c:Only by using the outside mirror.
note: Before every lane change, turn your head to quickly glance at the blind spot area that mirrors cannot show.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection, how should a driver proceed?
options: a:Assume other drivers will yield to you.,b:Maintain speed and proceed as usual.,c:Yield to the vehicle on the right and be prepared to stop to avoid collisions.
note: At uncontrolled intersections yield to the right and be ready to stop if necessary to avoid a crash.

question: You must pull over to the right edge of the road and allow an emergency vehicle to pass:
options: a:Only if it is following you.,b:Only if it is approaching from the opposite direction.,c:Regardless of its direction.
note: Whether an emergency vehicle is approaching from behind or the opposite direction, pull to the right and stop when safe to do so.

question: When you get into a car to drive, what should you adjust first?
options: a:The steering wheel.,b:Your seat.,c:The rearview mirror.
note: Adjust your seat first so you have a clear view and proper control, then set mirrors and steering wheel.

question: Which practice can help conserve gasoline?
options: a:Sitting in your driveway with the car running.,b:Accelerating quickly.,c:Slowing down gradually.
note: Avoiding sudden stops and starts and slowing gradually can improve fuel efficiency.

question: If an oncoming driver is heading toward you in your lane, what should you do?
options: a:Blow your horn,b:You blow your horn,c:It is required to blow your horn
note: Honk to attract attention, try to escape to the right, and brake firmly; swerving left risks a head-on collision with the other vehicle.

question: When a transit vehicle signals to re-enter traffic after stopping, you must:
options: a:Honk to warn it to hurry up.,b:Yield and allow it to merge back safely.,c:Move into the right lane without slowing.
note: Yield to transit vehicles re-entering traffic after passenger loading; change lanes, slow, or stop to allow safe re-entry.

question: On a two-lane road without bike lanes, how should you pass a bicyclist traveling in the same direction?
options: a:Only pass at traffic signals,b:Honk and pass closely to encourage them to move over,c:Pass rapidly without changing lanes,d:Slow down
note: Pass bicyclists like other vehicles but allow extra room—at least 3 feet—and only pass when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To change lanes safely you should:
options: a:Check your mirrors and signal,b:Signal,c:Use turn indicator
note: Before changing lanes, signal, check mirrors, and look over your shoulder to ensure your blind spot is clear.

question: Turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes is considered:
options: a:A good driving habit,b:A bad driving habit,c:Unnecessary and unsafe,d:Only for new drivers
note: Checking your blind spot by looking over your shoulder before lane changes or merging is an essential safety habit.

question: Distracted driving is:
options: a:Very uncommon.,b:Extremely risky behavior.,c:Nothing to be concerned about.
note: Distracted driving greatly increases crash risk for drivers, passengers, pedestrians, and other road users.

question: What do regulatory signs do?
options: a:Indicate nearby services,b:Warn of hazardous conditions,c:Serve as tourist information,d:Indicate what drivers must or must not do
note: Regulatory signs tell drivers the laws and rules for the area (e.g., speed limits, no turns, lane use restrictions) and are enforceable.

question: What does a green arrow signal mean?
options: a:A green arrow is only used on one-way streets,b:A green arrow allows you to go straight regardless of arrows,c:A green arrow is the same as a circular green for all movements,d:Traffic indicated by the arrow may proceed and must turn in the direction shown
note: A green arrow permits traffic in the indicated lane to proceed in the arrow’s direction; it controls that turn specifically.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does an advisory speed sign (speed restriction sign) typically indicate?
options: a:The maximum legal speed for the roadway.,b:The recommended safe speed for a specific area such as a curve or turn.,c:The speed drivers should use in heavy traffic.
note: Advisory speed signs provide a recommended speed for curves and other conditions; they are not necessarily the posted maximum but indicate safe speed for that feature.

question: Motorcycles are entitled to:
options: a:The bicycle lane.,b:The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.,c:Half the width of a lane.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the full width of a traffic lane just like other motor vehicles; do not share their lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You want to turn left at an intersection; the light is green but oncoming traffic is heavy. What should you do?
options: a:Use the next intersection to turn.,b:Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.,c:Wait in the intersection and complete your left turn when it is safe to do so.
note: If the light is green you may enter the intersection to wait for a safe gap to make a left turn; do not block crosswalks or impede traffic.

question: When driving through an area where children are playing, you should expect them to:
options: a:Know when it is safe to cross the street.,b:Stop at the curb before crossing the street.,c:Run out into the street without looking.
note: Children may not recognize danger; slow down and be prepared for them to run into the roadway without warning.

question: Why must you be especially alert for motorcycles?
options: a:They rarely use headlights.,b:Motorcyclists are less skilled than other drivers.,c:They are smaller and harder to see than cars.
note: Motorcycles are smaller and easier to hide in blind spots; their speed and distance can be hard to judge, so exercise extra caution.

question: As you approach an accident scene, what should you generally do?
options: a:Stop and gather around to watch the scene,b:Pull off and block traffic so emergency responders can access the area,c:Drive by slowly and record the incident on your phone,d:Keep your attention on driving and keep moving unless you are involved or emergency help has not arrived
note: Do not stop at an accident unless you are involved or emergency assistance hasn't arrived. Keep moving, watching for people or hazards.

question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights is approaching?
options: a:Continue driving but try to stay out of its way.,b:Pull over to the side of the road and come to a complete stop.,c:See if you can reach your destination before it catches you.
note: Yield to emergency vehicles by pulling to the right and stopping when safe; if in an intersection, clear it before pulling over.

question: Which actions can reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Ignore other drivers' behavior entirely.,b:Only obey posted speed limits.,c:Allow extra travel time and use proper signals.
note: Allowing more travel time, using signals, and obeying rules help reduce stress and aggressive driving incidents.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes you should:
options: a:Glance over your shoulder to check blind spots and signal in advance.,b:Signal at least 500 feet before your lane change in residential areas.,c:Rely solely on your mirrors.
note: Always check mirrors and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots; signal well in advance (about 100 feet in residential areas).

question: If your wheels slip off the road edge, you should:
options: a:Jerk the wheel to re-enter immediately.,b:Slow down gradually and steer back onto the pavement when safe.,c:Speed up and re-enter quickly.
note: Keep control, slow gently, and when safe turn the steering wheel to return to pavement — do not oversteer sharply.

question: When changing lanes, which should you NOT do?
options: a:Give a turn signal to indicate your intent.,b:Fail to check side and rearview mirrors.,c:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
note: Before changing lanes, always check mirrors, signal, and be aware of other drivers who may also move into that lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are required to signal every time you pull away from a curb.
options: a:True,b:False
note: Use your turn signal whenever you pull away from a curb to warn other road users of your movement.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing you should:
options: a:Ignore it if no train is visible.,b:Speed up to cross quickly.,c:Slow down
note: On approaching railroad crossings, slow, look, and be prepared to stop; stop 15–50 feet from tracks if lights flash or gates are down.

question: It is unlawful for a car to share a single lane with a motorcycle.
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE
note: Motorcycles have the right to occupy a full lane; cars must never try to share a lane with a motorcycle.

question: If your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement, what is the proper reaction?
options: a:Take your foot off the accelerator, steer parallel to the road, slow down, then gently steer back onto the pavement when safe.,b:Accelerate and steer back onto the road quickly.,c:Stop immediately on the shoulder.
note: Don’t panic: remove foot from accelerator, keep wheels parallel to the roadway, slow down, and when safe, steer gradually back onto the pavement after checking traffic.

question: Which of these may cause distracted driving?
options: a:Only eating,b:Only talking on the phone,c:Eating,d:Only using navigation systems
note: Any task that diverts attention, hands, or eyes from driving — such as eating, texting, or adjusting music — increases crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving in the left lane and want to move into the right lane. What should you do?
options: a:Check mirrors,b:Look in mirrors,c:Check rear view
note: When moving to the right, check mirrors, signal, and glance over your right shoulder to verify the blind spot is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road you must:
options: a:Flash your lights at oncoming traffic to warn them.,b:Use the shoulder to pass.,c:Move into the oncoming traffic lane and complete the pass safely.
note: Passing on a two-lane road requires entering the opposing lane; do so only when safe and legal.

question: Which technique helps avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?
options: a:Reduce your speed and increase following distance.,b:Add extra weight to improve traction.,c:Get off the highways as quickly as possible.
note: Slowing down and increasing following distance are the most important strategies for preventing crashes on icy or snowy roads.

question: A diamond-shaped sign serves as a:
options: a:Road hazard/warning sign.,b:School crossing sign.,c:Interstate route sign.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are used as warning signs to alert drivers to upcoming hazards or special driving conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as a vehicle to your right. You should:
options: a:Drive into the intersection and make the other vehicle stop.,b:Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.,c:Speed up and get through the intersection.
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously at an uncontrolled intersection, yield to the vehicle on your right.

question: Should you use high beams when driving in fog?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Use low beam headlights in fog; high beams can reflect back off the fog and impair your vision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left, what should you do?
options: a:Signal, move into the left lane if applicable, slow gradually, and watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians,b:Stop in the middle of the intersection to wait for a gap,c:Turn without signaling to avoid confusing other drivers,d:Accelerate briefly and then turn quickly
note: Signal 3–5 seconds in advance, position your vehicle properly, slow gradually, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, then turn when clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about speed is correct?
options: a:Speeding has no impact on crash severity.,b:Driving too slowly on some highways can be hazardous.,c:Speeding is safe if you are an experienced driver.
note: Driving too slowly can be dangerous because it may cause others to attempt risky passes; higher speeds also increase the risk and severity of crashes.

question: Which factor does NOT affect vehicle stopping distance?
options: a:Your reaction time.,b:The condition of your brakes.,c:The time of day.
note: Stopping distance depends on reaction time, vehicle/trail conditions, and brakes; time of day does not directly affect stopping distance.

question: When passing a large vehicle, what should a small vehicle driver be prepared for?
options: a:Loud noises only.,b:Wind gusts produced by the large vehicle.,c:Increased air pollution.
note: Large vehicles can create strong gusts of wind that may affect smaller vehicles; be prepared to make corrective steering actions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at an open (uncontrolled) intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:One driver may continue without stopping.,b:The driver on the left.,c:The driver on the right.
note: Yield to the vehicle on your right when both arrive at the same time at an uncontrolled intersection.

question: If you notice a defect that could affect your vehicle’s safe operation, what should you do?
options: a:Drive more slowly and postpone repairs,b:Only repair it if it fails during a trip,c:Wait until you can afford the repair,d:Correct the defect as soon as possible before driving
note: Any safety-related defect should be repaired promptly to ensure the vehicle remains safe to operate.

question: Smoking or preparing to smoke while driving:
options: a:Do not affect driving abilities.,b:Help maintain driver alertness.,c:Are distracting activities.
note: Smoking can distract you by taking your hands or eyes off the road, creating a driving hazard.

question: Is it lawful to drive at night using only your parking lights?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Driving at night with only parking lights is unlawful; headlights must be used when driving in the dark.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit in a residential area?
options: a:20 mph.,b:15 mph.,c:25 mph.
note: Unless a different speed is posted, the speed limit in business or residential areas is 25 mph.

question: “Highway hypnosis” can result from:
options: a:Too much sleep the night before a trip.,b:Frequent rest stops.,c:Staring at the roadway for long periods.
note: Highway hypnosis is a trance-like state caused by long periods of monotonous driving and lack of scanning; take breaks to stay alert.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who must you yield to?
options: a:Drivers who arrived before you.,b:Drivers who arrived after you.,c:Drivers on your left only.
note: At four-way stops, yield to vehicles that arrived before you and proceed in turn.

question: Why is it important to maintain a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:It prevents distractions from other vehicles.,b:It keeps traffic flowing at a steady pace.,c:It gives you time to react to unexpected actions by other road users.
note: Leaving plenty of space around your vehicle ensures you have time to react to mistakes or sudden moves by other drivers.

question: How can you avoid being in a truck or bus driver's blind spot?
options: a:Never pass them.,b:Avoid driving alongside them and do not tailgate.,c:Flash your lights at them to get their attention.
note: Large vehicles have significant blind spots; avoid lingering alongside them and do not tailgate to reduce collision risk.

question: If a vehicle comes toward you with high beams on and blinding headlights, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to pass quickly,b:Flash your high beams back to warn them,c:Keep looking at the lights to maintain lane position,d:Look away from the headlights toward the right edge of the road until the vehicle passes
note: Look toward the right edge of the road and avoid staring at the oncoming beams to reduce temporary blindness.

question: When approaching a flashing red traffic signal, a driver must:
options: a:Slow down at the light.,b:Merge to the right.,c:Stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when safe.
note: A flashing red signal requires a full stop; proceed only after yielding to other traffic and pedestrians when it is safe.

question: When driving in fog, you should use your low beam headlights:
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: Use low beams in fog; high beams reflect back into your eyes and reduce visibility.

question: A learner's permit allows practice driving while supervised by whom?
options: a:A licensed driver education teacher only.,b:An approved driving instructor,c:Any licensed driver.
note: Practice driving with a learner's permit is allowed only when accompanied by an approved instructor, a licensed parent or guardian, or a responsible licensed adult who signed for financial responsibility.

question: If there is an oncoming car on your left and a bicyclist on your right, what should you do?
options: a:Pull onto the shoulder between them,b:Try to split the space between them,c:Pass the bicyclist immediately and hope the oncoming car yields,d:Let the oncoming car pass first
note: When confronted with multiple hazards, handle them one at a time: let the oncoming car pass, then safely pass the bicyclist.

question: Which of these does NOT affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Your body weight.,b:How much time passes between drinks.,c:The type of alcoholic beverage you drink.
note: BAC depends on how much you drink, your body weight, and time between drinks; the beverage type does not change BAC.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is an allowable passing situation?
options: a:Passing by using the highway shoulder,b:Passing in a curve or on a hill because you think no vehicle is coming,c:Passing when your lane is next to a solid yellow line,d:Passing when the center line next to your lane is a broken yellow line and the passing lane is clear
note: You may pass when the line beside your lane is broken (dashed) and it is safe to do so; never pass on curves, hills, or shoulders.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning onto a street that has multiple lanes going in your direction, you should:
options: a:Turn into the lane closest to your original lane.,b:Turn into the middle lane.,c:Turn into the lane marked with an arrow.
note: When turning onto a multi-lane street, enter the lane nearest to the lane you came from and avoid changing lanes while turning.

question: Signs that warn drivers about hazardous conditions ahead are called:
options: a:Guide signs,b:Warning signs,c:Information signs,d:Regulatory signs
note: Warning signs alert drivers to potentially hazardous conditions or changes on the road so they can take appropriate action.

question: At a railroad crossing that has no flashing lights or gates, you should slow down, look, and listen.
options: a:True,b:False
note: Where no active warning devices exist, drivers must slow, look both ways, and listen for approaching trains before crossing.

question: What is a safe way to drive through a curve?
options: a:Slow down entering and accelerate gradually exiting.,b:Maintain constant speed throughout.,c:Speed up entering and slow down exiting.
note: Reduce speed before the curve and increase speed progressively as you exit to maintain control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to exceed the posted speed limit when passing another vehicle?
options: a:True,b:False
note: You may not legally exceed the posted speed limit even when passing another vehicle.

question: What should you do to avoid collisions caused by vehicles in your blind spots?
options: a:Rely solely on blind spot detection systems,b:Adjust your mirrors every five minutes while driving,c:Quickly turn your head and glance over your shoulder to check before changing lanes,d:Honk before changing lanes to warn other motorists
note: Visually checking blind spots by turning your head helps ensure there is no vehicle hidden from mirror view before you change lanes.

question: Are drivers always required to stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road?
options: a:True — but only during school hours,b:False — only drivers behind the bus must stop,c:False — only if children are present,d:True — drivers in both directions must stop for a stopped school bus with flashing red lights on a two-lane road
note: On two-lane roads, traffic in both directions must stop for a school bus that is loading or unloading with flashing red lights.

question: If you begin to feel sleepy while driving, the best action is to:
options: a:Open your window.,b:Get some coffee.,c:Stop driving and rest.
note: Driving while fatigued is dangerous; the safest option is to stop driving and rest or switch drivers.

question: Is a railroad crossbuck sign treated the same as a yield sign?
options: a:False,b:True
note: A crossbuck at a railroad crossing functions as a yield sign; drivers must yield the right-of-way to any approaching trains or railroad equipment.

question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, what must you do when turning?
options: a:You retain exclusive right-of-way to turn without yielding.,b:You may no longer turn; proceed only straight.,c:Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.
note: When a green arrow becomes a solid green, you may still turn but must yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic first.

question: Which of the following about seat belts and child restraints is correct?
options: a:An airbag can be dangerous to an infant or small child,b:You should never place an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.,c:Always ensure all passengers are using seat belts or appropriate child restraints (best single guidance).
note: Always fasten your seat belt and make sure children are in appropriate restraints; infants should not be placed in a front seat with an active airbag.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:When entering a highway where other cars are present.,b:When anything makes driving conditions less than ideal.,c:When you see a police car.
note: Reduce speed below the posted limit when the road is wet, visibility is poor, or other conditions make driving unsafe; you can be cited for driving too fast for conditions even if under the speed limit.

question: If a school bus is stopped with red lights flashing on a private road, must you stop?
options: a:False,b:True
note: When a bus has red lights flashing and the stop arm out, drivers on both public and private roads are required to stop.

question: If your vehicle begins to hydroplane (skid on water), should you immediately apply the brakes?
options: a:No — you should release the accelerator and steer to regain control,b:Yes — apply the brakes quickly,c:Yes — pump the brakes rapidly,d:Yes — shift into neutral and keep accelerating
note: If your vehicle is hydroplaning, do not slam on the brakes. Ease off the accelerator, steer smoothly to maintain control, and slow gradually.

question: If you must stop along the road at night, what should you do?
options: a:Turn off all lights,b:Turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low-beam headlights on,c:Use only your parking lights,d:Use high beams to warn other drivers
note: If stopped at night, leave low beams on and activate your emergency flashers so other road users can see you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road should:
options: a:Force their way into traffic.,b:Assume they have the right-of-way.,c:Yield to traffic already on the public road.
note: When entering from private property, yield to drivers already on the roadway and merge only when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should drivers do when approaching a steady red traffic light?
options: a:Drive through if there is no crossing traffic.,b:Come to a complete stop; right turns may be allowed unless prohibited.,c:Continue driving because they have the right-of-way.
note: A steady red requires a complete stop; drivers may turn right on red only if not prohibited and after yielding to others.

question: A leaking exhaust system can:
options: a:Cause excessive oil use.,b:Require your vehicle to have a tune-up sooner than normal.,c:Make you drowsy while driving because of fumes.
note: Exhaust leaks can allow toxic fumes into the cabin and cause drowsiness or carbon monoxide poisoning; repair leaks promptly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a steady green light, what must you do?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians and any other traffic with the right-of-way,b:Always come to a complete stop before turning,c:Honk to warn pedestrians,d:Turn without yielding if you think the way is clear
note: On a green light you may turn but must yield to pedestrians and other vehicles that have the right-of-way before turning.

question: What shape is a stop sign?
options: a:A rectangle,b:A diamond,c:An octagon,d:A circle
note: A stop sign is uniquely octagonal (eight-sided), indicating the driver must come to a complete stop.

question: If another vehicle may hit you, what should you do first?
options: a:Wave your arms to attract attention.,b:Turn on your emergency lights only.,c:Sound your horn to warn the other driver.
note: Use your horn to warn drivers or pedestrians when you believe a collision is imminent.

question: When passing a vehicle that has just parked on the side of the road, you should:
options: a:Speed up to pass quickly.,b:Assume the driver might open a door and proceed cautiously.,c:Slam on your brakes as you pass.
note: Assume a parked vehicle may have occupants opening doors or pulling away; use extra caution when passing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To enter a freeway you should:
options: a:Signal, yield to existing traffic, and enter at the same speed as traffic.,b:Signal and enter the freeway; freeway traffic must yield.,c:Drive slowly so you can check traffic.
note: Use the acceleration lane to match freeway speed, signal, and yield to traffic already on the freeway before merging.

question: What is the most important rule about speed management when driving through curves?
options: a:Drive at the posted limit through the entire curve and slow at the sharpest part.,b:Accelerate gently before you enter the curve.,c:Slow down before you enter the curve.
note: Because inertia makes turning more difficult, reduce speed before entering the curve to maintain control.

question: Which of the following is hardest to see at night?
options: a:Pavement markings,b:Other vehicles,c:Road signs,d:Pedestrians
note: Pedestrians are especially difficult to see at night compared to road signs or other roadside objects; extra caution is needed.

question: When stopped on an uphill slope you should:
options: a:Reduce following distance normally.,b:Always apply the parking brake only.,c:Allow a larger space cushion in front of you.
note: Allow extra space ahead on uphills in case the vehicle in front rolls back when traffic moves again.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection from different highways simultaneously, who yields?
options: a:The vehicle on the right yields to the left.,b:Either vehicle may proceed.,c:The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.
note: If two vehicles enter at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot when you are:
options: a:Pulling toward or away from a curb.,b:Changing lanes.,c:Turning left or right.
note: Always glance over your shoulder to check blind spots before changing lanes, turning, or moving toward or away from a curb.

question: If your power steering fails while driving, you should:
options: a:Honk your horn and turn off the ignition immediately.,b:Turn on hazards and brace yourself without slowing.,c:Work harder to steer
note: Power steering loss requires more effort to steer; reduce speed and safely pull off the road to stop.

question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:
options: a:A serious traffic safety problem.,b:Safe if you have only had a few drinks.,c:A minor traffic safety problem.
note: Driving while impaired by alcohol or drugs is a major safety hazard and can be deadly to you and others.

question: Which action helps prevent rear-end collisions?
options: a:Before stopping,b:Avoid sudden stops.,c:Release the gas pedal and allow your vehicle to slow before firmly applying the brakes.
note: To reduce the chance of a rear-end crash, ease off the accelerator to slow, then apply steady braking so following drivers have time to react.

question: On a road without sidewalks, which way should a pedestrian walk?
options: a:On the same side as the direction traffic is moving.,b:On the side with the lightest traffic.,c:Facing oncoming traffic (on the side facing traffic).
note: Pedestrians should walk on the side of the road facing oncoming traffic so they can see approaching vehicles in the lane nearest them.

question: A yellow traffic signal that flashes on and off means:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop and wait for a green light.,c:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
note: A flashing yellow light indicates you should slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution.

question: Drivers should recognize that large trucks:
options: a:Do not need more room to maneuver than passenger vehicles.,b:Can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.,c:Have large blind spots.
note: Large trucks have extensive blind spots and need more room to maneuver and stop; avoid lingering in their no-zones.

question: At dusk or on overcast days you should:
options: a:Turn on your headlights and use low beams when appropriate.,b:Drive using your four-way flashers.,c:Drive using only your parking lights.
note: Turn on headlights when visibility is reduced; use low beams within 1,000 feet of oncoming vehicles and 500 feet of vehicles you are following.

question: Why exercise extra caution near a pedestrian using a white cane?
options: a:They are necessarily deaf.,b:They are law enforcement personnel.,c:They are blind and may not see or hear you.
note: A white cane typically indicates a blind pedestrian; you must yield and proceed cautiously to avoid harm.

question: When you approach a railroad crossing with flashing signals, you should:
options: a:Stop and look for a train.,b:Slow down and look for a train.,c:Look for a train
note: If warning lights are flashing at a railroad crossing you must stop at a safe distance (no closer than 15 feet) and wait until the signals stop.

question: A motorist making a left turn must yield to a bicyclist entering the intersection from the opposite direction. True or False?
options: a:True,b:False
note: When turning left you must yield to oncoming bicyclists just as you would to oncoming motor vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver behind you wants to pass, how should you respond?
options: a:Drive at the same speed as before.,b:Speed up to prevent them from passing.,c:Slow down to give the other driver space to pass easily.
note: Slow down to create space in front of your vehicle so the other driver can complete the pass safely and quickly.

question: Signs indicating areas of public recreation and cultural interest are what color?
options: a:Brown.,b:Red.,c:Green.
note: Brown signs mark recreational, cultural, and historical sites to help travelers locate public recreation areas.

question: When riding in a vehicle, how should small children be secured?
options: a:Never allow a child to ride unless properly fastened into an appropriate child safety seat.,b:They will be safe if they are standing on the floor in the back of the vehicle.,c:They may be safely held by a strong adult.
note: Children who are too small to use regular safety belts must be secured in an appropriate child restraint. No adult can safely hold a child during a crash or sudden stop; always use the proper child seat.

question: Which traffic light indicates you should slow down and proceed with caution?
options: a:A steady yellow light,b:A steady green light,c:A flashing yellow light,d:A flashing red light
note: A flashing yellow signal warns drivers to slow down, proceed with caution, and be prepared to stop if necessary.

question: Which statement about drowsy drivers is correct?
options: a:Opening a window or turning up the radio will reliably keep them alert,b:Drinking coffee permanently cures drowsiness while driving,c:Drowsy drivers can perform so poorly that they may appear to be intoxicated,d:Drowsiness only affects unskilled drivers
note: Drowsiness impairs judgment and reaction time; it can make driving performance similar to that of drunk drivers. Temporary measures rarely work.

question: Are you permitted to drive around or under a railroad crossing gate that is being lowered or raised?
options: a:Yes,b:You yes,c:No — never drive around or under a lowering or raising gate.
note: Flashing lights, bells, or lowered gates signal an approaching train; never go around or under moving gates.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before moving from the right lane into the left lane on a multilane highway, what should you do?
options: a:Look in your side mirror for traffic and turn on your signal.,b:Look over your left shoulder for vehicles in your blind spot before changing lanes.,c:Look only in your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
note: Always check mirrors and then quickly look over your shoulder toward the lane you intend to enter to check for vehicles in your blind spot; signal every time you change lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers may not pass from either side of which centerline?
options: a:Combination solid and broken yellow.,b:Single broken yellow.,c:Double solid yellow.
note: A double solid yellow centerline prohibits passing from either direction.

question: What does a driver's left arm extended upward indicate?
options: a:They intend to turn right.,b:They intend to turn left.,c:They intend to stop.
note: A left arm pointing upward is the hand signal for a right turn; be alert if following that driver.

question: Work zones may be which of the following?
options: a:Never require drivers to slow down or use extra caution.,b:Always stationary and marked with black and white signs.,c:Marked with orange signs and may be moving or stationary.
note: Work zones are often marked with orange signs and can be stationary or involve moving operations; you must slow down and pay extra attention when driving through them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your slow driving causes traffic to back up on a two-lane, two-way road, what should you do?
options: a:Keep driving at the same speed.,b:Pull off the road to let traffic pass.,c:Speed up to restore traffic flow.
note: If you are impeding traffic on a two-lane, two-way road, you must safely pull off to allow other vehicles to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on a freeway, what is the correct action?
options: a:Make a last-second turn from your lane,b:Stop and reverse back to the exit,c:Continue to the next exit or safe turnaround and do not back up on the shoulder,d:Cross the median to return to the exit
note: If you miss an exit, continue to the next exit or another safe location to turn around. Never back up on a freeway or shoulder.

question: Which describes a good defensive driver?
options: a:Drives slowly at all times.,b:Looks ahead for the actions of other drivers and anticipates problems.,c:Travels at a constant speed regardless of conditions.
note: A defensive driver watches for the actions of others and anticipates potential problems; they adapt speed and behavior to conditions.

question: Your vehicle's brake lights tell other drivers that you are:
options: a:Slowing down or stopping.,b:Changing lanes.,c:Making a turn.
note: Brake lights indicate to drivers behind you that you are slowing or stopping; keep them in working order.

question: How should drivers react to a flashing red traffic light?
options: a:Treat it like a stop sign: come to a complete stop, then proceed when safe,b:Drive through if no crossing traffic is present,c:Only stop if a police officer is nearby,d:Slow down and proceed without stopping
note: A flashing red light requires a full stop; then proceed when the way is clear, just as with a stop sign.

question: Should you avoid driving alongside large vehicles for long periods?
options: a:True — avoid lingering beside large vehicles because of their blind spots,b:False — large vehicles have small blind spots,c:False — it is safer to stay beside them,d:True — because they always drive slower
note: Large vehicles have extensive blind spots on both sides; it's safer to either drop back or pass quickly.

question: Should drivers continually work to improve driving and observation skills?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Because driving always involves risk, continually improving observation and driving skills increases safety.

question: What color are signs that tell the distance to the next highway exit?
options: a:Red with white letters,b:Yellow with black letters,c:Green with white letters
note: Directional and destination signs, such as those indicating distances to exits, are green with white lettering.

question: Does the type of alcoholic beverage (beer, wine, mixed drinks) determine how impaired you will be?
options: a:Yes — beer has no effect on reflexes,b:No — impairment depends on how much alcohol is in the bloodstream,c:Yes — mixed drinks are always more impairing than beer,d:Yes — wine is less impairing than beer
note: Impairment depends on blood alcohol concentration, not the beverage type; any alcohol can impair reflexes and judgment.

question: What is a blind spot?
options: a:The area directly behind your vehicle.,b:An area you cannot see without moving your head.,c:What you can see in your rearview mirror.
note: Blind spots are areas beside or behind your vehicle that are not visible in mirrors and require a head check.

question: If you hit an unattended parked car and cannot find the owner, you must:
options: a:Wait until the police arrive and do nothing else.,b:Drive away after doing as much as you can.,c:Leave a written note with your name
note: If you cannot locate the owner of a vehicle you struck, leave a written notice with your contact information and circumstances.

question: A red arrow displayed on a traffic signal means:
options: a:Stop and remain stopped until a green light or green arrow appears.,b:A driver must proceed slowly through the intersection.,c:A driver must stop and then proceed when the way is clear.
note: A red arrow requires drivers to stop and remain stopped until a green light or green arrow is displayed.

question: If you drink socially, what helps ensure a safe trip home?
options: a:Take a cold shower before driving.,b:Drink coffee before driving.,c:Ride with a sober friend.
note: Only a sober ride home prevents driving impaired; coffee or showers do not lower BAC.

question: An octagonal traffic sign always means:
options: a:Hospital ahead,b:Stop,c:Yield,d:Speed limit
note: The eight-sided (octagon) sign is reserved for STOP signs; approaching drivers must come to a complete stop.

question: Can there be times when 10 mph is too fast to drive safely?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Drive below posted limits when conditions require it; sometimes you must drive as slowly as 10 mph for safety.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:Not all railroad crossings are equipped with flashing lights and gates,b:You are allowed to go around a lowered gate if you do it quickly,c:You never need to stop for a flagger,d:Gates and lights are always present at public crossings
note: Some crossings lack gates or lights, so always be prepared to stop when approaching a crossing and obey all warnings and flaggers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Other drivers who are already in the intersection only.,b:Only to vehicles turning right.,c:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.
note: When turning left you must yield to oncoming vehicles as well as pedestrians, bicyclists, and others already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: During school hours, what is the default speed limit in a school zone unless posted otherwise?
options: a:15 mph.,b:20 mph.,c:25 mph.
note: Unless posted differently, the speed limit is 20 mph in a school zone during school hours when children are present or flashing lights are active.

question: If a crossing guard directs traffic in a school zone, you must:
options: a:Follow the crossing guard's directions.,b:Follow what surrounding vehicles do instead.,c:Assume the guard has no authority.
note: Obey crossing guards and traffic control in school zones; they are directing traffic for safety.

question: Which statement about driving on a wet roadway is correct?
options: a:As you drive faster, your tires become less effective at removing water.,b:Water does not affect cars with good tires.,c:Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
note: The faster you travel on wet pavement, the less effective tires are at keeping contact with the road; high speeds can lead to hydroplaning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to change lanes, which checks should you perform?
options: a:Quickly turn your head to check for other vehicles only.,b:Only check your side view mirror.,c:Check side view and rearview mirrors
note: Before changing lanes, check side and rearview mirrors and then glance over your shoulder to make sure no vehicle is in your blind spot.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Are drivers required to yield to pedestrians in crosswalks?
options: a:False — drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks (this statement is false),b:True — pedestrians always have right-of-way under all conditions,c:True — drivers must yield to pedestrians in marked and some unmarked crosswalks,d:False — drivers are not required to yield everywhere
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in marked crosswalks and to pedestrians in unmarked crosswalks on the driver’s side where no traffic signals exist.

question: What color lines divide lanes moving in the same direction?
options: a:White lines.,b:Yellow lines.,c:Red lines.
note: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction; broken white lines may be crossed to pass, yellow lines separate opposite directions.

question: When parallel parking between two vehicles, what should you do first?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the left.,b:Turn your wheels to the right.,c:Pull up even with the vehicle directly ahead of the space.
note: After finding a space, check traffic and signal, then stop parallel to the car ahead of the desired space before beginning to back in.

question: How can alcoholic beverages affect you?
options: a:They have no effect on judgment,b:They can slow reaction time,c:They only affect people who rarely drink,d:They improve coordination
note: Alcohol reduces reaction time, impairs judgment and coordination, and can give a false sense of confidence, increasing crash risk.

question: How should drivers respond to a steady yellow traffic light?
options: a:Accelerate to avoid a red light.,b:Continue driving because you have the right-of-way.,c:Slow to a stop
note: A steady yellow indicates the light is about to turn red; stop if it is safe to do so unless you are already in the intersection.

question: If your vehicle does not have ABS and you must stop quickly, what should you do?
options: a:Lightly tap the brakes.,b:Firmly pump the brakes.,c:Hold the brake pedal down hard.
note: For vehicles without ABS, pumping the brakes helps achieve a quick stop while maintaining some steering control in an emergency.

question: Which steps help prevent hydroplaning?
options: a:Only check tread depth occasionally,b:Drive faster to cut through water,c:Ensure tires have good tread,d:Only inflate tires properly
note: Good tire tread, correct tire pressure, and reduced speeds in wet conditions all reduce the risk of hydroplaning.

question: Which type of action is most likely to cause a crash?
options: a:Only taking your hands off the wheel,b:Anything that takes your attention away from driving,c:Only taking your eyes off the road,d:Only talking to passengers
note: Distractions that remove your attention, eyes, or hands from driving increase crash risk; any of these actions can be dangerous.

question: What does the slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?
options: a:A reflective orange triangle.,b:A circular green sign.,c:A rectangular red sign.
note: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle indicating the vehicle typically travels 25 mph or less.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Does 'yield' sometimes require you to stop if you cannot merge safely?
options: a:True,b:False
note: When you must yield and cannot safely merge into traffic, you are required to stop until it is safe to proceed.

question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children, what should you do?
options: a:Do not proceed until the children wave to you.,b:Watch for children walking along the side of the road before proceeding.,c:Accelerate quickly to clear the area.
note: After a bus stops with its stop arm out and lights flashing, watch carefully for children near the road and proceed only when it is safe.

question: A solid white line down the center of a two-lane road indicates:
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction; a solid white line discourages or prohibits lane changes.

question: If an aggressive driver is tailing you or behaving dangerously, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to prevent them from passing,b:Brake-check them so they back off,c:Stare at the driver to intimidate them,d:Move out of their way and avoid interaction
note: If someone is driving aggressively, try to get out of their way, avoid eye contact, and do not engage or challenge them.

question: If your vehicle with ABS starts to lose traction, drivers should:
options: a:Pump the brakes manually.,b:Release the brake pedal immediately.,c:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
note: With ABS, press and hold the brake firmly; the system will pulse the brakes as needed to maintain control.

question: Does a “Merging lanes” sign require drivers to be prepared to change lanes or allow others to merge?
options: a:True — but only on one-way streets,b:True — drivers should be prepared to change lanes or allow merging traffic,c:False — it is informational only,d:False — it indicates lane ends only
note: A merging lanes sign warns that two lanes will become one and drivers should adjust their speed or position to merge safely.

question: Orange-colored traffic signs typically indicate:
options: a:Work zone signs.,b:School zone signs.,c:Regulatory signs.
note: Orange signs are commonly used in highway work zones to warn drivers about road work or construction activities.

question: How can you prevent drowsiness on long trips?
options: a:Keep the radio off.,b:Drive slower continuously.,c:Stop regularly to rest and stretch.
note: Schedule regular stops to rest and stretch; naps or overnight stays are best if drowsy.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your interstate exit, what should you do?
options: a:Quickly cut across lanes to reach the exit.,b:Make a sudden U-turn across traffic to reach it.,c:Continue to the next exit and do not attempt to turn around.
note: If you pass an exit on the interstate, proceed to the next exit rather than making unsafe maneuvers.

question: At an intersection, what does a flashing red light require you to do?
options: a:Stop only if traffic is present.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Come to a complete stop
note: A flashing red light has the same meaning as a stop sign: stop completely, check traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.

question: About how much alcohol does the average person's body process per hour?
options: a:One drink an hour.,b:Two drinks an hour.,c:Three drinks an hour.
note: On average the body metabolizes roughly one standard drink per hour, though many factors affect impairment.

question: Which statement about winter driving is NOT true?
options: a:Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.,b:Winter is the most difficult driving season.,c:Checking your antifreeze and washer fluid is important.
note: You should never use cruise control on slippery surfaces like snow or ice; winter requires extra caution and vehicle maintenance checks.

question: Who is required to use a properly fastened safety belt in Utah?
options: a:Only the driver,b:Only passengers younger than 16,c:Only passengers older than 18,d:All occupants of the vehicle
note: In Utah all vehicle occupants must wear seat belts. Drivers may be cited if they or passengers under 16 are not restrained; passengers 16+ may also be cited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a 'Merging traffic' sign on the freeway, you should:
options: a:Make room by changing lanes or adjusting speed to allow merging traffic.,b:Honk at incoming traffic.,c:Always remain at your present speed.
note: On multi-lane roads make room for entering vehicles by moving over or adjusting your speed so merging traffic can safely enter.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How far must you be able to be seen from both directions before making a U-turn?
options: a:200 feet.,b:500 feet.,c:100 feet.
note: Never make a U-turn where you cannot be seen from 500 feet in both directions, such as near a hilltop or curve.

question: When backing up, how should you check behind your vehicle?
options: a:Flash your lights continuously while backing,b:Rely solely on mirrors and sensors,c:Open your door and step out every time,d:Turn and look through the rear window over your shoulder and do not rely only on mirrors
note: Before and while backing, turn to look through the rear window to see what mirrors and sensors might miss.

question: At night when another vehicle approaches from the opposite direction, your headlights should be:
options: a:Turned off and use parking lights.,b:Set to high beam.,c:Set to low beam.
note: Use low beams when approaching other vehicles at night to avoid blinding them.

question: A red flashing traffic light has the same meaning as a:
options: a:Solid red light.,b:Stop sign.,c:Yield sign.
note: A flashing red light is equivalent to a stop sign: come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.

question: A child under eight years old and shorter than what height must be in an approved child safety seat?
options: a:72 inches,b:60 inches,c:57 inches
note: Utah law requires children under eight years old who are shorter than 57 inches to be secured in an approved child safety seat until a seat belt fits properly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving on an interstate, before changing lanes you should:
options: a:Always use cruise control.,b:Signal,c:Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
note: On interstates, signal well in advance and check mirrors and blind spots before changing lanes; only stop on the shoulder for emergencies.

question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line indicate?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid line.,b:Passing is allowed from either direction.,c:Passing is allowed from the lane next to the broken line.
note: When a broken yellow is alongside a solid yellow, vehicles on the broken-line side may pass when safe; the solid side may not.

question: How does a wet or icy road affect stopping distance?
options: a:It only affects stopping at night.,b:It decreases stopping distance.,c:It increases stopping distance.
note: Stopping distances are longer on wet, icy, loose gravel, or otherwise poor road surfaces.

question: If someone has consumed alcohol, which remedy will help them sober up quickly?
options: a:Fresh air and exercise will sober them up quickly,b:Tomato juice will speed sobriety,c:Only the passage of time will eliminate the influence of alcohol,d:Hot coffee will remove alcohol from the bloodstream
note: Nothing speeds the elimination of alcohol from the body except time; coffee, fresh air, or other remedies do not reduce blood alcohol concentration.

question: A properly adjusted seat belt should fit how?
options: a:Is loose.,b:Is buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.,c:Is hidden beneath the seat.
note: Lap belts should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen; shoulder belts should lie comfortably across the chest.

question: What is true about drivers who have consumed alcohol before driving?
options: a:They are better drivers because they are more cautious than sober drivers.,b:They are always aware of the risks they are taking.,c:They do not have sufficient control over their bodies
note: Alcohol impairs judgment, vision, concentration, and reaction time; alcohol consumption before driving prevents adequate control of vehicle and mental functions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-way, two-lane road, when is passing unsafe?
options: a:When the car ahead is disabled.,b:When turning into a driveway.,c:When you cannot return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
note: You may pass only if you can do so safely: see clearly, return before oncoming traffic, and have adequate speed to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Drivers may proceed without stopping if they feel safe,b:The first vehicle to arrive should proceed first,c:The vehicle on the left always goes first,d:The last vehicle to arrive has priority
note: At a four-way stop, vehicles stop in all directions. The vehicle that arrives first should proceed first; if two arrive together, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving on a highway divided by two solid yellow lines. Which action is allowed?
options: a:Cross these lines to pass other vehicles,b:Cross these lines under no circumstances.,c:Cross these lines only to make a left turn into or from an alley
note: Double solid yellow lines mark a roadway where passing is prohibited in both directions; you may cross them only to make a left turn into or from an alley, private road, driveway, or to turn left when permitted.

question: Defensive driving means:
options: a:Following the vehicle ahead at a close distance.,b:Identifying dangerous driving situations and taking action to avoid accidents.,c:Defending yourself by getting ahead of poor drivers in traffic.
note: Defensive driving involves recognizing hazards early and taking proactive steps to avoid collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must yield when a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light?
options: a:Whoever started moving last,b:The pedestrian must yield to the turning vehicle,c:The driver turning must yield to the pedestrian,d:The vehicle that is slower must yield
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing the roadway, even at intersections without traffic signals.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to stop or park on the shoulder of a freeway?
options: a:Any time if you turn on emergency flashers,b:If part of the vehicle is off the roadway,c:To check a map or get directions,d:Only in an emergency
note: Parking on the freeway shoulder is prohibited except in emergencies. Use your flashers and move to a safe area.

question: When driving in poor weather, what should you do to maintain safety?
options: a:Tailgate slower vehicles to encourage them to speed up,b:Increase your following distance to allow more stopping time,c:Decrease your following distance to get off the road quicker,d:Maintain the same following distance as in clear weather
note: In bad weather increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead to give yourself extra time to react and stop.

question: What does a single dashed white line separating traffic indicate?
options: a:Lanes moving in the same direction that may be crossed to pass.,b:Drivers may not pass under any circumstances.,c:Lanes move in opposite directions.
note: A dashed white line separates lanes traveling the same way and may be crossed to pass or change lanes when safe.

question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, how should you position your front wheels?
options: a:Keep the front wheels straight and set the parking brake.,b:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,c:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
note: On an uphill with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if the brakes fail.

question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, you must:
options: a:Turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.,b:Close the door and leave the engine running.,c:Leave the key in the ignition for a short time.
note: When leaving a vehicle unattended, stop the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

question: Nighttime is the safest time for cyclists to ride their bikes.
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: Bicycles are harder to see at night even with lights and reflectors; extra caution is needed after dark.

question: If you see an animal on the road, what should you do?
options: a:Pass as closely as possible to clear the way.,b:Ignore it and maintain speed.,c:Pass slowly and cautiously to avoid startling it.
note: Approach animals with extreme caution; slow down and pass slowly to avoid frightening them into unpredictable movement.

question: If another driver cuts you off, the best immediate reaction is to:
options: a:Flash your high beams at the driver.,b:Let it go and continue driving safely.,c:Pull next to the driver and yell at them.
note: Avoid road rage and unsafe responses; let it go and maintain safe driving behavior.

question: If a train is near enough to be dangerous, what must you do?
options: a:Not cross the tracks until the train has fully passed.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Cross the tracks if no signals are active.
note: Do not cross railroad tracks if a train is close enough to pose a danger; always stop when warning devices or conditions require it.

question: A flashing red traffic signal means:
options: a:The traffic signal is broken.,b:The same thing as a stop sign.,c:You do not have to come to a complete stop.
note: A flashing red light has the same meaning as a stop sign: come to a complete stop, yield, then go when safe.

question: A Class D license authorizes you to operate a vehicle that weighs up to which of the following?
options: a:26,000 pounds.,b:36,000 pounds.,c:33,000 pounds.,d:40,000 pounds.
