note: A Class D regular operator license permits operation of personal vehicles up to 26,000 pounds GVWR; heavier vehicles require a different class of license.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are stopped by a police officer, you should:
options: a:Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.,b:Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach.,c:Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.
note: Remain in the vehicle with hands visible and wait for the officer to approach; only retrieve documents when asked.

question: A single broken white line down the center of a two-lane road indicates:
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers may pass when it is safe.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction; you may change lanes or pass when it is safe.

question: Before switching on the ignition you should:
options: a:Buckle your safety belt and ensure all passengers have done likewise.,b:Be sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.,c:Be sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
note: Develop a routine to buckle your own seat belt and confirm that all passengers are belted before starting the vehicle.

question: What does a single dashed yellow centerline mean?
options: a:Both lanes travel in the same direction.,b:Drivers may pass when it is safe to do so.,c:Drivers may not pass at any time.
note: A single dashed yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions and indicates passing is allowed when safe and without interfering with oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic signals at an intersection are out due to a power outage, you should:
options: a:Park and wait for power to be restored.,b:Treat the intersection as a four-way stop and proceed when it is your turn.,c:Use hand signals to direct traffic.
note: When traffic lights are out, drivers should yield in the same manner as at a four-way stop and proceed only when it is safe to do so.

question: If your vehicle is blocking traffic after an accident, what should you do if possible?
options: a:Never move it under any circumstances,b:Move it off the traveled portion of the roadway,c:Wait for police to move it for you,d:Leave it and walk away
note: After a minor collision move your vehicle off the road if it is safe to do so; but do not leave the scene without exchanging information or rendering aid.

question: As a pedestrian, what is the safest action when vehicles are approaching?
options: a:Enter a crosswalk at any time because drivers must stop.,b:Always insist on the right-of-way over a vehicle when in a crosswalk.,c:Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
note: Do not enter a street or crosswalk if vehicles are approaching. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a nearby vehicle may not be able to stop in time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do speed limit signs indicate?
options: a:Potential driving speeds for the area.,b:The maximum or minimum speed that is legally allowed to be driven.,c:The speed drivers should drive in heavy traffic.
note: Speed limit signs show the maximum (or minimum) legal speed under ideal conditions; you must reduce speed when conditions require it.

question: If you are being tailgated, what is the best response?
options: a:Accelerate to increase the gap,b:Move to the right if possible; if not,c:Brake abruptly to teach them a lesson,d:Ignore them and maintain your speed no matter what
note: If rear-ended is possible, move over if safe; if you cannot, slow gradually when safe to encourage the tailgater to pass. Never brake suddenly.

question: On slippery roads you should:
options: a:Drive as you would on dry roads.,b:Increase your following distance.,c:Use alternate routes.
note: Slippery conditions increase stopping distances, so increase your following distance to allow more time to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to other drivers?
options: a:When entering a street from a garage, driveway, or alley.,b:When your traffic signal is a green arrow.,c:When they are on a road to your left and you have reached an unmarked intersection at the same time.
note: You must yield when entering the roadway from a driveway, alley, or garage and also yield to pedestrians on intersecting sidewalks.

question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?
options: a:Carbon monoxide poisoning.,b:A loss of hearing.,c:Pollution.
note: A leaking exhaust can allow carbon monoxide to enter the passenger compartment, which can be fatal; repair leaks immediately.

question: A steady yellow traffic signal means which light will soon appear?
options: a:A flashing red will soon appear,b:A steady green will soon appear,c:A steady red light will soon appear,d:A flashing yellow will soon appear
note: A steady yellow warns that the signal is about to turn red, so prepare to stop if it is safe to do so.

question: A diamond-shaped traffic sign generally:
options: a:Alerts drivers to school zones.,b:Alerts drivers to public recreation areas.,c:Warns of existing or possible hazards.
note: Diamond-shaped signs (often yellow or orange) warn drivers of existing or potential hazards on or near the roadway.

question: If confronted by an aggressive driver, what is the recommended response?
options: a:Engage in an argument at the next stop,b:Avoid eye contact,c:Cut them off to slow them down,d:Retaliate by tailgating them
note: Remain calm, avoid confrontation, slow down and allow the aggressive driver to pass; do not retaliate or engage.

question: When a traffic signal turns green, what should you do first?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians and any traffic still in the intersection.,b:Accelerate as fast as possible.,c:Back up slowly.
note: A green light permits you to go but you must first yield to pedestrians and vehicles that remain in the intersection.

question: A driver should never pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk. Is this true?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Never pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk; doing so could endanger pedestrians who may be crossing ahead of the stopped vehicle.

question: If a traffic signal turns from green to solid yellow as you approach, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to get through before it turns red.,b:Treat it the same as a caution sign and continue.,c:Stop before entering the intersection unless you are too close to stop safely.
note: A steady yellow warns the light is changing to red; stop if you can safely do so, otherwise continue through with caution.

question: When parking uphill next to a curb on a two-way street, how should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Keep your wheels straight,b:Turn so the rear wheel rests on the curb,c:Turn your steering wheel to the left so the front right tire rests against the curb,d:Turn your steering wheel to the right
note: Parking uphill with a curb, turn the wheel away from the curb (to the left on right-side parking) so the vehicle will roll into the curb if brakes fail.

question: You are involved in an accident. Which immediate action is required?
options: a:Help the injured.,b:Call the police.,c:Stop immediately.
note: Stop at the scene immediately; if possible, move out of traffic, render aid if you can do so safely, and call emergency services.

question: How can you avoid alcohol-related crashes?
options: a:Simply say you will not drink if someone offers you a drink.,b:Call a taxi only after you start drinking.,c:Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive.
note: The surest way to avoid drunk driving is to decide beforehand not to drive after drinking and make alternate transportation plans.

question: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings:
options: a:Are merely suggestions.,b:Must always be obeyed.,c:Must be followed only when there is other traffic.
note: Traffic control devices regulate traffic flow and must be obeyed to drive safely and legally.

question: A red traffic signal means you must:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop before entering the intersection or crosswalk.,c:Stop only if pedestrians are present.
note: A red light requires stopping at the stop line or, if none, before entering the crosswalk or intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Do pedestrians in crosswalks and at intersections always have the right-of-way?
options: a:False — pedestrians have the right-of-way in many situations, but not always (for example, when they disobey traffic signals),b:True — they always do under all conditions,c:False — drivers always have the right-of-way,d:True — except at marked crosswalks
note: Pedestrians generally have the right-of-way when crossing at intersections or crosswalks, but must also obey traffic signals and laws.

question: What defines an inattentive driver?
options: a:Watching only the vehicle directly ahead of them.,b:Maintaining eye contact with a passenger during a conversation.,c:Daydreaming or staring at objects off the roadway while driving.
note: Inattentive driving includes distractions like daydreaming, reading, or looking away from the roadway.

question: When may you cross solid yellow lines?
options: a:To pass traffic moving in your direction.,b:Only to make a turn.,c:At any time of day.
note: Solid yellow lines generally cannot be crossed except when making a permitted turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before passing another vehicle you should:
options: a:Signal after changing lanes.,b:Signal early enough for other drivers to know your intentions.,c:Signal just before changing lanes.
note: Signal early enough to inform other drivers of your intent, then check mirrors and blind spots before passing.

question: How should you check your blind spot when changing lanes to the left?
options: a:Turn on your left turn signal and rely on it,b:Look straight ahead only,c:Check your right side mirror,d:Glance over your left shoulder
note: Before moving left, look over your left shoulder to check the blind spot; mirrors alone may not reveal vehicles there.

question: When making a turn, you must do what with your speed?
options: a:Reduce it so you can maintain control.,b:Increase it to clear the intersection.,c:Keep it unchanged.
note: Slow to an appropriate speed before a turn to maintain control and stay in your lane.

question: How should you regard railroad crossings?
options: a:Safe places to park a car.,b:Dangerous and always approached with caution.,c:Safe to cross because trains are unlikely.
note: Railroad crossings are always potentially hazardous; look, listen, and obey all signs and signals before crossing.

question: What does the term “No zone” refer to around large vehicles?
options: a:A lane closed for construction,b:A roadway where stereo systems are restricted,c:Areas of reduced visibility (blind spots) around trucks and buses,d:A special speed zone
note: The “No zone” refers to blind spot areas around large trucks and buses where smaller vehicles may not be visible in the truck’s mirrors.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing without flashing warning signals or gates, you should:
options: a:Always stop before crossing the tracks.,b:Prepare to yield to any approaching train at the crossing.,c:Cross the tracks immediately and as quickly as possible.
note: Approach such crossings with caution, look and listen for trains, and only cross when you are sure no trains are approaching.

question: A “Reduced speed, 35 mph” sign indicates what?
options: a:The reduced speed sign is advisory only and begins after the next sign,b:You have plenty of distance to slow down before the zone,c:The reduced speed applies only if police are present,d:The new speed limit of 35 mph begins at that sign
note: When a reduced speed sign posts a new limit, the new speed begins at the sign itself and must be obeyed from that point.

question: What is the legal BAC limit to drive in Utah?
options: a:0.08 percent.,b:0.02 percent.,c:0.05 percent.
note: Utah's legal per se BAC limit for most drivers is 0.05 percent; impairment rules also apply even below that level.

question: What is the only effective way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Allow your body time to eliminate the alcohol.,b:Drink coffee to sober up.,c:Exercise to speed alcohol removal.
note: Only time removes alcohol from your system; coffee, showers, and exercise do not lower BAC.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane should you start a left turn on a multilane one-way street or highway?
options: a:Start from the middle of the intersection.,b:Start from the left lane.,c:Start from the right lane.
note: To turn left from a multilane one-way street or highway, begin the turn from the left lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you slow down when exiting a highway?
options: a:After you have moved into the exit lane.,b:On the main road, just before the exit lane.,c:Once you see a toll booth.
note: Enter the exit lane in advance and only begin slowing down after you are in the exit lane; do not brake on the main travel lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a highway from an entrance ramp, you should generally:
options: a:Merge without signaling to move quickly,b:Enter very slowly to avoid disturbing traffic,c:Accelerate to match the speed of traffic and merge when safe,d:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a clear gap
note: Use the acceleration lane to reach highway speed, signal, look for a gap, and merge smoothly into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what circumstance may you cross double solid yellow lines?
options: a:To pass a slow-moving truck.,b:To pass another car.,c:To turn into a driveway or to make a left turn where permitted.
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate no passing; you may cross only to turn left into or from a driveway, private road, alley, or where left turns are allowed.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is traveling in your area, you should:
options: a:Speed up to avoid the emergency vehicle.,b:Stop your vehicle immediately and prevent them from passing.,c:Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path of travel.
note: When safe, pull to the side of the road and stop to allow emergency vehicles a clear path; follow local laws on yielding to emergency vehicles.

question: How can you ensure your physical condition doesn't impair your driving?
options: a:Only drive when feeling perfectly rested.,b:Know medicine effects,c:Drive faster to reduce exposure time.
note: Be aware of medications, your physical limitations, and maintain health to drive safely.

question: Is it true that the faster your speed, the longer it takes to stop?
options: a:Only true for heavy vehicles,b:Only true when roads are wet,c:False,d:True
note: As speed increases, stopping distances grow, giving you less time to react to unexpected situations.

question: Which of the following is a recommended practice for driving safely at night?
options: a:Make sure your headlights are working properly.,b:Increase your following distance.,c:Do not drive if you are tired.
note: Night driving reduces visibility; increase following distance, avoid driving while tired, and ensure headlights are functional to improve safety.

question: How should you drive on slippery roads?
options: a:Maintain posted speed regardless of conditions,b:Slow down and drive more cautiously than the posted speed,c:Drive faster to get through quickly,d:Tailgate the vehicle ahead to reduce spray
note: Reduce speed at the first sign of rain, snow, or ice and drive more slowly than the posted speed when conditions are poor.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing that only has a crossbuck sign, you should:
options: a:Approach all tracks with extreme caution and cross only when you know no train is coming.,b:Turn your radio down to hear if a train is approaching.,c:Only continue once cleared to do so by a flagger, if applicable.
note: Crossbucks indicate a railroad crossing; always look and listen for trains and do not cross until the tracks are clear.

question: What does a regulatory sign with a red circle and slash indicate?
options: a:That some drivers must yield to others.,b:That the specified action is prohibited.,c:That drivers should come to a complete stop.
note: A red circle with a slash on top of a symbol indicates the action shown is forbidden; such regulatory signs prohibit specific actions.

question: When should you use your headlights due to limited visibility?
options: a:Only at night.,b:Only when you can see 500 feet ahead.,c:Any time conditions prevent you from seeing at least 1
note: Turn on headlights whenever conditions reduce visibility to less than 1,000 feet so you and others can see better.

question: How should you pass a bicyclist safely?
options: a:Honk to alert the bicyclist to move over.,b:Drive in the bike lane until you can pass.,c:Slow down and give as much space as possible.
note: When passing bicycles, slow down and leave wide clearance; do not crowd or pass quickly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following takes precedence over the others?
options: a:A police officer directing traffic,b:A steady red light,c:A stop sign,d:Pavement markings
note: Directions given by authorized traffic officers override signs, signals, and pavement markings.

question: If you have a tire blowout while driving, what should you do first?
options: a:Keep accelerating to maintain control,b:Slam on your brakes immediately,c:Ease off the accelerator,d:Turn the vehicle off while moving
note: If a tire blows out, steer firmly, release the accelerator, avoid hard braking, slow gradually, and then pull off the roadway safely.

question: What color are guide/destination signs and their lettering?
options: a:Yellow background with black letters,b:Green background with white letters,c:Red background with white letters
note: Guide signs have a green background with white letters or symbols and provide directional and mileage information.

question: When interacting with pedestrians, a driver must:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way only when the pedestrian is legally entitled to it.,b:Always yield the right-of-way,c:Make sure the pedestrian is aware of their vehicle.
note: Drivers must do everything possible to avoid striking pedestrians and should yield to them even if they are crossing where they should not be.

question: If a pedestrian starts crossing in front of you, what should you do?
options: a:Flash your lights to warn them to hurry.,b:Speed up and pass ahead of them.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop
note: Always slow and be ready to stop for pedestrians, especially children and those in crosswalks; yield the right-of-way.

question: As alcohol builds up in your bloodstream, it:
options: a:Begins to metabolize itself more quickly.,b:Makes you feel less confident.,c:Slows down your reactions.
note: Alcohol impairs reaction time and judgement; it also increases confidence while decreasing driving ability.

question: How must drivers respond to a stopped school bus with its stop arm extended and red lights flashing?
options: a:Proceed if you think children are clear,b:Slow down and pass carefully,c:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the bus resumes motion or the stop arm is withdrawn,d:Honk to alert any children
note: When a school bus displays its stop signal, all drivers must stop and remain stopped until the bus moves or the stop signal is withdrawn.

question: What should motorists do when driving near a cyclist?
options: a:Honk to make the cyclist move over,b:Share the lane without increasing following distance,c:Maintain a safe operating distance and be especially cautious,d:Assume the cyclist will yield right-of-way
note: Drivers must take care around bicyclists and keep a safe distance, giving them room when passing.

question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, you should:
options: a:Maintain your current speed and steer straight.,b:Try to steer straight while gradually slowing by removing your foot from the gas pedal,c:Brake hard immediately.
note: Hold the wheel firmly, keep the vehicle straight, ease off the gas and brake gently once control is regained, then pull off the road safely.

question: On a divided multilane highway when an emergency vehicle approaches, how should you respond?
options: a:Stop as quickly as you can in your lane.,b:Disregard the signal if other lanes are available.,c:Slow down
note: You must slow down, move to give a clear path for the emergency vehicle, and stop; do not try to outrun it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is the posted maximum speed limit always the fastest safe speed you can drive?
options: a:True,b:False
note: The posted maximum is the fastest legal speed under ideal conditions; you must drive slower when conditions require it (e.g., slippery roads, poor visibility).

question: When driving in rain, which lights should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Parking lights only.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: Use low beam headlights in rain to improve visibility without causing glare for other drivers.

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical effect of drinking alcohol?
options: a:Slower reflexes and reaction time.,b:Increased alertness.,c:Distorted judgement of speed and distance.
note: Alcohol reduces alertness, slows reaction time, and distorts judgment; it does not increase alertness.

question: Should you use high beam headlights while driving in fog?
options: a:No — high beams can reflect back and reduce visibility (False),b:Yes — high beams improve visibility in fog (True),c:Either is fine depending on the road,d:Use high beams with fog lights
note: High beams reflect off fog and reduce visibility; use low beams or fog lights if provided when driving in fog.

question: What do pentagonal (five-sided) road signs indicate?
options: a:Speed limits.,b:School zones.,c:No passing zones.
note: Pentagonal signs identify school zones and school crossings; be extra alert for children and pedestrians near schools.

question: Orange signs in work zones indicate what?
options: a:They indicate scenic routes,b:They mark parking restrictions,c:They warn drivers of construction or maintenance work areas,d:They designate school zones
note: Orange, often diamond-shaped signs are used to warn drivers about construction and maintenance work areas.

question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and wait for the light to change.,b:Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.,c:Drive carefully through the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow signal means slow down and proceed with caution while scanning for cross traffic and pedestrians.

question: What type of sign requires drivers to obey the instruction it indicates?
options: a:Warning signs.,b:Information signs.,c:Regulatory signs.
note: Regulatory signs (e.g., speed limits, stop signs) require compliance; failure to obey can be penalized.

question: How do blind spots change with vehicle size?
options: a:Larger vehicles have smaller blind spots,b:Large vehicles have no blind spots due to mirrors,c:Larger vehicles have larger blind spots,d:All vehicles have the same blind spot size
note: The larger the vehicle, the larger the blind spots. Trucks and large SUVs have significant zones that drivers may not see in mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may cautiously continue through an intersection with a yellow light if:
options: a:There are pedestrians crossing.,b:An emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.,c:You are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.
note: If you are already within the intersection when the light turns yellow or cannot stop safely before entering, continue through carefully.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are required to stop your vehicle under which conditions?
options: a:Where there is a red light only.,b:At a stop sign,c:At an intersection with a stop sign only.
note: Required stops include stop signs, red lights (including flashing red), and whenever a traffic officer directs you to stop.

question: If you must drive in fog, you should:
options: a:Drive at the maximum posted speed.,b:Turn on your low-beam headlights.,c:Use your hazard lights.
note: Use low-beam headlights (not high beams) and slow down when visibility is reduced by fog or heavy precipitation.

question: Road surfaces are especially slippery during which period of a rainstorm?
options: a:When it has been raining for an hour or more.,b:The day after it rains.,c:For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
note: Roads are often most slippery in the first 10–15 minutes of rain as oils rise to the surface; exercise caution and reduce speed.

question: Which road condition most affects your ability to stop?
options: a:The condition of the road surface.,b:Signal lights.,c:The time of day.
note: Road surface conditions (wet, icy, gravel) greatly influence braking distance and vehicle control.

question: Which of the following can impair a person's ability to drive?
options: a:Only prescription medications,b:Alcohol,c:Only having little sleep,d:Only illegal drugs
note: Alcohol, legal and illegal drugs, and drowsiness can all impair driving performance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: While waiting in an intersection to complete a left turn, how should you position your wheels?
options: a:Signal and keep your wheels straight so you won’t be pushed into oncoming traffic if struck from behind,b:Signal and keep your wheels turned left,c:Flash headlights to warn oncoming drivers,d:Honk to get other drivers to stop
note: Keep wheels straight while waiting to turn left so a rear-end collision won't push you into opposing traffic.

question: What is the most common color for warning signs?
options: a:Yellow,b:Green,c:Red
note: Warning signs are typically diamond-shaped and yellow with black markings to alert drivers to unexpected conditions ahead.

question: Under what conditions may you drive around a lowered railroad gate?
options: a:If you can see there is no train approaching,b:Under no circumstances,c:Only when the lights stop flashing,d:When the train has passed and the gate is fully raised
note: You must never drive around a lowered gate. Only proceed when signals are cleared and the gate is raised and it is safe to cross.

question: What is the single most effective action to reduce your risk of serious injury or death in a crash?
options: a:Limit driving to weekdays.,b:Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.,c:Wear your seat belt.
note: Wearing a seat belt greatly reduces the chance of death or serious injury in a crash and is the most effective protective action.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it illegal to cross a single broken white or yellow line?
options: a:When turning left into a driveway.,b:When the car ahead is disabled.,c:When crossing would interfere with other traffic.
note: You may cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes only if it can be done safely and without interfering with other traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection where you wish to turn but are not in the proper lane, you should:
options: a:Turn on your blinker and make the turn from your current lane.,b:Drive to the next intersection and make the turn from the proper lane.,c:Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
note: Do not make last-minute lane changes; continue to the next intersection and turn from the correct lane.

question: When approaching a steady green traffic light, drivers should:
options: a:Continue driving unless there are vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection.,b:Stop if a police officer is nearby.,c:Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
note: With a steady green light you may proceed but must yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection and be prepared to stop if the light changes.

question: Is parking in handicap access aisles next to accessible stalls allowed?
options: a:True — if you have a permit,b:True — for short stops only,c:False — parking in handicap access aisles is prohibited,d:True — if nobody is using the access aisle
note: Access aisles are required for mobility devices and lifts and must be kept clear; parking there is prohibited.

question: What is a common cause of crashes?
options: a:Consistently checking mirrors and blind spots.,b:Yielding the right-of-way correctly.,c:Driving too fast for conditions.
note: Excessive speed for conditions is a frequent crash cause; always adjust speed to conditions.

question: Driving while distracted usually causes the driver to:
options: a:React more quickly to hazards.,b:React more slowly to hazards.,c:Drive faster than usual.
note: Distractions delay your perception and reaction time, increasing crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Passing is prohibited in which places?
options: a:On hills,b:At intersections only.,c:On hills and curves only.
note: Passing in locations where visibility or safety is limited (hills, curves, intersections, railroad crossings) is unlawful and unsafe.

question: A common telltale sign of a drunk driver is:
options: a:Driving more slowly than the normal traffic flow.,b:Weaving between lanes.,c:Making quick and sudden stops.
note: Erratic behavior such as weaving between lanes is a typical indicator of impaired driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is passing prohibited?
options: a:Whenever you are near an intersection.,b:Only when school bus lights are flashing.,c:On a hill or curve where visibility is limited.
note: Passing is prohibited on hills, curves, intersections, before railroad crossings, and other no-passing zones; you also must not pass a stopped school bus with flashing reds unless on the opposite side of a divided highway.

question: You approach a railroad crossing and hear or see no train; when must you still stop?
options: a:Only if crossing lights are flashing.,b:Never stop if you don't see a train.,c:If a stop sign is posted.
note: Stop at railroad crossings when a stop sign is posted, the gate is down, lights flash, a flagger directs you, or a train is visible or too close.

question: Are drivers allowed to pass a school bus when its red lights are flashing?
options: a:False,b:True
note: When a school bus displays flashing red lights, all drivers approaching must stop until the lights are turned off, except on opposite sides of a divided highway with a median.

question: What should drivers do when approaching a flashing yellow traffic light?
options: a:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly,b:Ignore it if no other cars are visible,c:Stop like at a stop sign,d:Slow down and proceed with caution
note: A flashing yellow light warns of a hazard; you should slow and proceed with caution, being prepared to stop.

question: What is the most common mistake drivers make while backing?
options: a:Using their horn too much,b:Failing to look both ways behind them,c:Backing too slowly,d:Only relying on rear-view cameras and not mirrors
note: Drivers often fail to turn and look through the rear window; mirrors do not provide a complete view, so physically looking back is important.

question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:Parking lights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:High beam headlights.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow; high beams will reduce visibility by reflecting back.

question: What should you do before passing another vehicle?
options: a:Re-enter your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.,b:Honk your horn at least three times.,c:Check your mirrors and blind spots
note: Before passing, verify mirrors and blind spots, signal, and only move back into the lane when you can see the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror.

question: Which is a good practice when driving on major highways?
options: a:Fix cruise control and focus on one distant point,b:Stay alert and be ready to react to hazards,c:Rely on automatic systems without scanning,d:Keep your eyes fixed straight ahead for long periods
note: On highways avoid highway hypnosis: stay alert, keep your eyes moving, and be ready to react to unexpected hazards.

question: How does alcohol affect your driving skills and judgment?
options: a:It has no effect on driving skills or judgment.,b:It harms both driving skills and judgment.,c:It helps driving skills but harms your judgment.
note: Alcohol impairs many abilities needed for safe driving, such as reaction time, vision, and judgment, and it lowers inhibitions.

question: When driving near heavy trucks, other road users must allow for what characteristic of large vehicles?
options: a:Their decreased stopping distance,b:Their increased stopping distance,c:Their reduced blind spots,d:Their smaller turning radius
note: Large vehicles require greater stopping distance; smaller vehicles should avoid remaining in blind spots and give extra space.

question: What can happen if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?
options: a:The alcohol will help the medicine cure a cold.,b:The combination could multiply the effects of the alcohol or medicine.,c:The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.
note: Mixing alcohol with medications can increase the impairing effects of one or both substances, sometimes greatly increasing risk.

question: To relieve fatigue on a long trip, you should:
options: a:Do occasional arm exercises while driving.,b:Drive with one eye open and one closed.,c:Stop and rest every two hours.
note: To prevent drowsiness, take breaks at least every two hours and rest if you feel drowsy.

question: At a railroad crossing with multiple tracks, when should you proceed after a train passes?
options: a:As soon as the first train passes,b:Only after you have a clear view of all tracks and are sure no other trains are coming,c:Drive around any remaining gates if they appear safe,d:Stop on the first track and watch for another train
note: Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks; another train may be approaching on a different track.

question: If involved in an accident, what should a driver do at the scene?
options: a:Stop near the scene, avoid standing in traffic lanes, and turn off ignitions of wrecked vehicles.,b:Leave the scene if no one appears injured.,c:Stand in traffic lanes to direct drivers around the wreck.
note: Stop at or near the scene, move vehicles out of traffic if possible, avoid standing in lanes, and turn off ignitions of wrecked cars.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:One driver may continue without stopping.,b:The driver on the left.,c:The driver on the right.
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously, yield to the driver on your right; proceed when it is safe.

question: What is the best response to a tailgater?
options: a:Change lanes or gradually slow to encourage them to pass.,b:Slam on your brakes to force them back.,c:Speed up to widen the gap.
note: If someone is following too closely, safely move aside or slow to let them pass rather than reacting aggressively.

question: What is commonly used on some highways to direct drivers into the proper lanes for turning?
options: a:Flashing yellow lights,b:Flashing red lights,c:Arrows painted or displayed for lanes.
note: Arrows (painted or signal arrows) indicate which lanes are designated for turning or going straight.

question: You want to back out of your driveway and see children playing nearby. Before moving the vehicle you should:
options: a:Exit the car and walk to the rear to ensure the way is clear.,b:Rev your engine to warn the children.,c:Sound your horn so the children will hear you.
note: When children are nearby, get out and check behind your vehicle rather than relying solely on mirrors or cameras before backing up.

question: Using a cellphone to talk or text while driving significantly increases your crash risk.
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE
note: Using a phone while driving is a distraction and increases your chance of being involved in a crash.

question: You come to an intersection with a flashing red light. What is the correct action?
options: a:Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.,b:Stop at the intersection and wait for a green light.,c:Come to a full stop
note: A flashing red signal has the same meaning as a stop sign: stop completely, then go when safe.

question: If a bicyclist disobeys traffic laws, what can happen?
options: a:They can be ticketed,b:They are immune from citations,c:They will always receive only a warning,d:They must be escorted by police
note: Bicyclists have the same duties and responsibilities as motorists; they can be cited for violating traffic laws.

question: When is it appropriate to sound your horn?
options: a:To alert others if you have lost control or to warn of immediate danger,b:To express frustration at a slow driver,c:When passing every vehicle in city traffic,d:To greet a friend on the sidewalk
note: Use your horn to warn others of danger or to avoid a collision; do not use it out of anger or habit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is driving below the posted speed limit illegal?
options: a:Only when driving in rural areas.,b:When in heavy traffic in a construction zone.,c:When driving so slowly that it disrupts the normal flow of traffic.
note: Driving so slowly that you impede traffic flow is illegal and you may be cited for obstructing traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A good rule to remember about passing is:
options: a:Try to get to the front of slow-moving traffic to see better.,b:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only as necessary.,c:Pass on the right whenever possible.
note: Limit passing to necessary situations, obey speed limits, and drive with the flow of traffic to reduce collision risk.

question: A driver who is taking a non-prescription drug should:
options: a:Continue to drive regardless of any warning labels.,b:Drink alcohol instead.,c:Read the labels on the drug before driving.
note: Many over-the-counter medicines can affect driving ability; read labels and consult a pharmacist or doctor if unsure.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?
options: a:Stay in the driver's blind spot.,b:Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.,c:Keep a steady pace.
note: Don't remain in another vehicle's blind spot; either move ahead or fall back so the driver can see you in their mirrors.

question: In vertical traffic lights, what is the order from top to bottom?
options: a:Red,b:Green,c:You red
note: On vertically arranged signals, red is on top, yellow in the middle, and green on the bottom.

question: Stop lines (solid white lines across lanes) indicate you must stop at:
options: a:Next to churches and schools.,b:At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.,c:In curves and on hills.
note: Stop lines mark the exact location where approaching drivers must stop at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.

question: Regulatory traffic signs are usually what color and must always be obeyed?
options: a:Green,b:White,c:Blue
note: Regulatory signs (such as speed limits and lane controls) are typically white with black markings and must be obeyed.

question: If the accelerator gets stuck while you're driving, what is the correct immediate response?
options: a:Shift to neutral, apply steady pressure on the brake, steer to a safe area, then turn off the engine,b:Try to reach under the pedal and pull it up while driving fast,c:Shift to park immediately at highway speed,d:Turn off the ignition while moving in traffic
note: If the accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road, shift to neutral, brake steadily, pull off safely, and then turn off the engine.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and keep moving in your lane.,b:Pull to the right curb and stop.,c:Keep driving in your lane.
note: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle using lights or siren, immediately pull to the side of the road and stop to allow it to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The space you need to cross traffic safely depends on which factors?
options: a:Whether you used your turn signal.,b:Road conditions,c:Presence of a stop sign only.
note: The space required to cross depends on road and weather conditions plus the amount of oncoming traffic.

question: What does a single broken yellow centerline indicate on a two-lane road?
options: a:Lanes move in the same direction and passing is prohibited,b:Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is prohibited,c:It marks an emergency lane,d:Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is permitted when safe
note: A dashed yellow line between opposing lanes means passing is allowed from either side when it is safe to do so.

question: If another driver is attempting to pass your vehicle, you should:
options: a:Pull off the road.,b:Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to allow a safe pass.,c:Signal to the other driver when it is safe for them to pass.
note: When being passed, maintain your lane and speed or adjust slightly to allow the passing vehicle to re-enter your lane safely when it is clear.

question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal indicate?
options: a:Drivers may turn in the direction indicated by the arrow.,b:This type of signal is never used.,c:It has the same meaning as a circular red traffic light — stop and do not turn.
note: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light for the indicated movement: stop and do not proceed in the arrow's direction.

question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing that has no signals directing traffic?
options: a:Always bring the car to a complete stop.,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop if a train is approaching.,c:All railroad crossings have signals so you will never encounter this situation.
note: When there are no lights or gates, approach with caution, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop if necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left onto a one-way street, which lane should you enter?
options: a:Either lane at random.,b:The rightmost lane.,c:The lane closest to your previous lane.
note: When turning onto a one-way street, enter the lane closest to the lane you came from, unless signs indicate otherwise.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection and opposing traffic blocks your view, what should you do?
options: a:Wait until you can see all the lanes you must cross before beginning your turn,b:Begin the turn when the first lane clears and accelerate through the rest,c:Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across,d:Lean out and inch forward into the intersection
note: Do not start a left turn until you can see that every lane you need to cross is clear and you can complete the turn safely.

question: At a school crossing sign you should:
options: a:Always sound your horn when you see children.,b:Watch for children and be ready to stop.,c:Always stop
note: Be alert when approaching school crossings and be prepared to stop for children in or about to enter the crosswalk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-lane, two-way road when is it permissible to drive on the left half?
options: a:In a legal passing zone when passing a vehicle traveling in the same direction.,b:When passing in a curve.,c:When passing another vehicle at a railroad crossing.
note: You may use the left half only when you are passing in a legal passing zone and it is safe relative to oncoming traffic.

question: Which is NOT part of stopping distance calculation?
options: a:Braking distance.,b:Reaction distance.,c:Steering ability.
note: Stopping distance consists of perception, reaction, and braking distances; steering ability is not directly a component.

question: Which statement about changing weather and driving is true?
options: a:Be particularly aware of vehicles behind you in bad weather.,b:Only slow down when driving in rain and fog.,c:All of the above.
note: If weather changes, adjust your driving (slow down in rain/fog) and be aware of vehicles behind you that may not be driving to conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, which vehicle has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle on the left has the right-of-way,b:The vehicle approaching from the right has the right-of-way,c:The larger vehicle always has the right-of-way,d:The vehicle that honks first has the right-of-way
note: At intersections without signs or signals, yield to vehicles approaching from your right when you arrive simultaneously.

question: Which of the following can impair your driving?
options: a:Only alcohol,b:Only illegal drugs,c:Only prescription medications,d:Marijuana
note: Many substances — illegal drugs, prescription medications, over-the-counter medicines, and marijuana — can impair driving ability.

question: What do pennant-shaped traffic signs indicate?
options: a:Speed limits.,b:No passing zones.,c:School zones.
note: Pennant-shaped signs mark no passing zones; the shape and text indicate that passing is prohibited.

question: If an oncoming vehicle is using high beams and doesn't dim them, you should look toward which part of the road?
options: a:Either side,b:The center,c:The right side.
note: Glance toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded by oncoming high beams while maintaining your lane position.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering a roundabout you must slow down and yield to which road users?
options: a:Bicyclists and pedestrians in or near the roundabout.,b:Vehicles already in the roundabout.,c:All of the above.
note: When entering a roundabout you must yield to vehicles already in it as well as to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing or near the roundabout.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A posted speed limit indicates what?
options: a:The speed only commercial vehicles must follow,b:The recommended speed when traffic is heavy,c:The maximum or minimum legal speed under ideal conditions,d:The suggested speed for hazardous conditions
note: The speed limit is the maximum (or minimum) legal speed under normal/ideal conditions; you must drive slower when conditions warrant.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Does a double solid yellow line allow passing from either direction?
options: a:True,b:False
note: A double solid yellow line means it is illegal to cross the centerline from either direction to pass.

question: How can you avoid making emergency stops in traffic?
options: a:Look ahead and maintain a safe following distance.,b:Honk frequently to keep others aware.,c:Drive only in the right lane.
note: Maintaining good spacing and scanning ahead reduces the need for sudden emergency stops.

question: If you're upset or angry when you get to your car, what should you do?
options: a:Play loud music to distract yourself,b:Take a few minutes to calm down before driving home,c:Drink coffee to become more alert,d:Drive fast to let off steam
note: Drivers who are emotionally upset should cool off before driving. Driving while angry or distracted is dangerous.

question: A lack of sleep affects driving ability in a way most similar to which of the following?
options: a:The effects of alcohol on driving,b:The effects of amphetamines,c:Feeling angry while driving,d:Taking cold medication
note: Fatigue impairs judgment and reaction time similarly to alcohol; being awake 18–24 hours can have effects comparable to low-to-moderate BAC levels.

question: What should you do when approaching railroad tracks?
options: a:Look and listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop,b:Speed up to beat the train,c:Drive around lowered gates if no train is sighted,d:Honk and proceed if you think it's safe
note: Approach crossings cautiously: look and listen for trains, obey signals, and be ready to stop if necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before making a turn?
options: a:Flash your headlights before turning,b:Increase your speed to complete the turn,c:Use your turn signal several seconds in advance,d:Turn the wheel sharply then signal
note: Activate your turn signal about three to four seconds before the turn so other road users know your intentions.

question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching, what should you do?
options: a:Proceed slowly and allow it to pass in traffic.,b:Stop immediately in your lane and let it pass.,c:Drive as far to the right as safely possible and stop.
note: On two-lane or undivided highways, immediately and safely move to the right side of the road and stop for an approaching emergency vehicle using lights or siren.

question: When driving in fog, you should use your high beam headlights. True or False?
options: a:False,b:True
note: High beams in fog reflect off the moisture and reduce visibility; use low beams instead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an intersection is blocked by traffic ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.,b:Stay out of the intersection until you can completely pass through.,c:Proceed slowly until the traffic moves.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it completely; blocking intersections is illegal and dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is signaling before turning, changing lanes, or pulling from a curb required?
options: a:It is necessary only if other traffic is present.,b:It is required only during the maneuver,c:It is required by law and is a good driving habit.
note: You must signal at least 100 feet before turning or changing lanes; signaling informs other road users of your intentions and is legally required.

question: What are the usual colors for warning signs that indicate hazards ahead?
options: a:Black symbols or letters on a yellow background.,b:White letters on a blue background.,c:Black symbols on a white background.
note: Warning signs are typically yellow with black lettering or symbols; work-zone warning signs are orange with black lettering.

question: You may drive across a dashed white line when:
options: a:At any time.,b:Only during daylight hours.,c:When it is safe to change lanes.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction; cross them only when it is safe to change lanes or pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, when should you return to your lane?
options: a:Return to the driving lane when there is enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.,b:Remain in the left lane if you intend to turn left.,c:Return to the right side immediately regardless of distance.
note: After passing, move back into your lane only when you can see the entire passed vehicle in your rearview mirror and it is safe to do so.

question: Motorists are required to yield to pedestrians even if the pedestrian is crossing against the traffic signal. True or False?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Drivers must do everything possible to avoid striking pedestrians and should yield to them even if the pedestrian is crossing improperly.

question: You notice the driver ahead is driving with one hand and talking to a passenger. What should you do?
options: a:Avoid following the driver's example.,b:Know that the other driver is reducing their safety margin by being inattentive.,c:Give that vehicle extra space.
note: If a nearby driver appears distracted, allow extra space because their risk of causing a crash is higher.

question: When there are two railroad tracks, and one train passes, what should you do?
options: a:Assume it's safe once the first train passes.,b:Always stop at the crossing regardless.,c:Look for another train on the other track before proceeding.
note: When multiple tracks exist, wait until you are sure no other trains are approaching on any track before crossing.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline mean?
options: a:You may pass when safe from either direction.,b:Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not permitted.,c:Lanes move in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate opposite flows of traffic and prohibit passing from either direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A broken yellow centerline indicates what about the road?
options: a:The road is under repair.,b:You are on a one-way road.,c:You are on a two-way road.
note: Yellow centerlines separate opposite directions of travel; a broken yellow line means passing is permitted when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive together, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The car on the left proceeds first.,b:The largest vehicle always has priority.,c:The vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.
note: If two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection simultaneously, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

question: Which factors influence the effects of alcohol on you?
options: a:Amount of food in the stomach, body weight, and time between drinks.,b:The color of the drink.,c:Your level of physical fitness only.
note: BAC and impairment are influenced by how much you drink, your weight, time between drinks, and whether you've eaten; fitness does not prevent intoxication.

question: If your tire suddenly blows out while driving, what is the recommended immediate action?
options: a:Accelerate to stabilize the vehicle,b:Hold the steering wheel firmly,c:Turn the engine off immediately while moving,d:Slam on the brakes and pull hard to the shoulder
note: Grip the wheel, avoid hard braking, gradually slow down, and steer to keep the vehicle in your lane before pulling over safely.

question: What should be your first reaction to reduced visibility?
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Turn on windshield wipers first.,c:Turn on interior lights.
note: When visibility decreases, slowing down should be your immediate response to increase safety.

question: Two solid white lines across a traffic lane mark a crosswalk. Which statement is correct?
options: a:Pedestrians must yield to turning vehicles,b:No one has right-of-way in a crosswalk,c:Motor vehicles always have right-of-way in crosswalks,d:When pedestrians are in crosswalks
note: Crosswalk markings indicate where pedestrians should cross; drivers must stop for pedestrians in crosswalks and yield to them.

question: A steady yellow traffic light means you should:
options: a:Go.,b:Slow down and prepare to stop.,c:Yield to other cars.
note: A steady yellow light indicates the light is about to turn red; slow down and prepare to stop unless you are already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is a possible maximum speed limit on some rural interstates in Utah?
options: a:65 mph.,b:80 mph.,c:50 mph.
note: Rural interstate speed limits in Utah can vary and may include 65, 70, 75, or 80 mph depending on location — always follow posted limits.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, what should drivers do?
options: a:Obey the officer's directions instead of the traffic signal.,b:Follow the directions indicated by the traffic light.,c:Honk at the officer if you disagree.
note: When a law enforcement officer is directing traffic, their directions take precedence over traffic signals and signs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver's left arm and hand extended downward indicates the driver plans to:
options: a:Stop.,b:Turn left.,c:Turn right.
note: A left arm extended downward is the hand signal drivers use to indicate they intend to stop. Adjust your driving accordingly when following a vehicle signaling this way.

question: Do ramps and bridges freeze before the main road surface?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Ramps and bridges can ice over sooner than regular roadways because their surfaces are exposed to air on both sides, so use extra caution.

question: Is it legal and safe to drive under or around a lowered railroad gate?
options: a:Yes — if you are in a hurry,b:Only if directed by another motorist,c:Yes — if you saw the train pass by,d:No — never drive through
note: It is both illegal and very dangerous to drive through, around, or under lowered railroad crossing gates.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving much slower than the posted speed and causing traffic to back up on a two-lane road, what should you do?
options: a:Always stay in the left lane to slow traffic,b:Speed up above the limit to keep traffic flowing,c:Pull off the road when safe and let other vehicles pass,d:Refuse to let anyone pass because you have the right-of-way
note: If you are moving so slowly that vehicles are backing up, you are required to safely pull off and allow traffic to pass.

question: What is the effect of taking drugs together with alcohol?
options: a:It increases the risk of causing a crash,b:It is no more dangerous than alcohol alone,c:It reduces the effect of alcohol,d:It only affects inexperienced drivers
note: Combining alcohol with drugs (prescription, over-the-counter, or illegal) can multiply impairing effects and increase crash risk.

question: Which road sections tend to freeze quickly and require extra caution?
options: a:Curvy sections of road.,b:Sections shaded by trees or buildings.,c:Roads in direct sunlight.
note: Shaded areas freeze faster and are the last to dry; take special care on these spots in cold or wet weather.

question: Where is parking unlawful?
options: a:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.,b:Anywhere in a parking lot.,c:Always on a hill.
note: Many places prohibit parking, including crosswalks and bike lanes; when street parking, stay within 12 inches of the curb.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering interstate traffic from an entrance or acceleration ramp should:
options: a:Force their way into traffic if necessary.,b:Expect other drivers to yield to them.,c:Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
note: Drivers entering an interstate should yield to vehicles already on the highway and merge safely when a gap exists.

question: When must you stop for a school bus?
options: a:Only if the bus is directly in front of you,b:When its red lights are flashing and you are on a two-lane road going either direction,c:Only if children are visible on the road,d:Only when you are behind the bus
note: When a school bus displays flashing red lights and a stop arm, vehicles in both directions on a two-lane road must stop and remain stopped.

question: Compared with daytime driving, night driving is generally:
options: a:No more or less dangerous.,b:More dangerous.,c:Less dangerous.
note: Night driving is more hazardous because visibility is reduced and drivers are more likely to be impaired or tired.

question: When can a licensed driver under 18 carry non-immediate-family passengers?
options: a:As soon as they receive their license.,b:Only after turning 17.,c:After holding their license for six months.
note: In Utah, drivers under 18 generally may not carry non-family passengers until they've had their license for six months, with some exceptions.

question: Which behavior helps prevent crashes with other road users?
options: a:Communicating with other road users by signaling and using your horn when appropriate,b:Ignoring other drivers and focusing only on your path,c:Driving only on side streets to avoid traffic,d:Maintaining silence to avoid startling pedestrians
note: Communicate your intentions (signals, lights, horn when needed) so other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians can anticipate your actions.
